15 languages appear in the language panel on the reverse.
Along with Hindi (front) and English (front), the note represents 17 languages in total.

teacher_understanding.question: How many languages does the page count, and where?
teacher_understanding.answer: It counts 15 in the reverse language panel, plus Hindi and English on the front, giving 17 in total.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are 15 and 17 not contradictory?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fifteen refers to the reverse panel alone; seventeen includes the two front languages as well.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this language arrangement help users?
teacher_understanding.answer: Displaying the denomination in multiple languages helps readers from different language backgrounds recognise the note's value.

prerequisites: front and reverse of a note
p009-i13.exam_note: Common distinction: 15 in the panel versus 17 in total.

terms.plain_meaning: note के एक हिस्से में कई भाषाओं में लिखा हुआ मूल्य
terms.everyday_image: एक ही कीमत को अलग-अलग भाषाओं में लिखी छोटी सूची

why_chain.step: Users read different languages.
The note displays its value through multiple languages, with the page counting 15 plus two.

unpack.example_or_place: Front: Hindi and English; reverse: 15-language panel.
unpack.consequence: Keep the panel count separate from the total count.
unpack.visual_verb: Flip the note and add 15 + 2 = 17.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse this count with the number of constitutionally scheduled languages.

teacher_understanding.question: What watermark does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies a watermark depicting Mahatma Gandhi as a major security feature.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is a watermark located?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is formed within the note paper, rather than being merely an ordinary surface-printed portrait.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it be examined?
teacher_understanding.answer: Holding the note against light reveals differences in light transmission that form the watermark image.

p009-i15.exam_note: Do not confuse the watermark with the ordinary printed portrait.

terms.plain_meaning: paper के अंदर बना हल्का चित्र जो रोशनी के सामने दिखता है
terms.everyday_image: note को बल्ब के सामने पकड़कर छिपा चेहरा देखना

why_chain.step: An ordinary printed copy can resemble a note's surface.
An image formed within the paper adds a different authentication check.

unpack.example_or_place: Mahatma Gandhi watermark on a note.
unpack.consequence: Use transmitted light, not just surface appearance.
unpack.visual_verb: Lift the note toward light and reveal the portrait.
unpack.level_extra: Features should be checked together, not as a single conclusive test.

teacher_understanding.question: What inscriptions does the security thread carry according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page lists “भारत”, “RBI”, and the denomination.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the security thread?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is incorporated into the note paper as a narrow security element.

teacher_understanding.question: How does checking the thread improve authentication?
teacher_understanding.answer: The user examines a specialised element and its lettering, rather than accepting any dark line drawn on paper as a genuine thread.

p009-i16.exam_note: Retain all three listed inscriptions; designs can vary.

terms.plain_meaning: note के paper में लगी सुरक्षा की पतली पट्टी
terms.everyday_image: कागज़ के बीच से जाती पतली line को पास से देखना

terms.plain_meaning: note पर लिखा रुपये का मूल्य

why_chain.step: A copied surface design may look convincing.
A specialised thread and its inscriptions offer an additional check.

unpack.example_or_place: Thread carrying “भारत”, “RBI” and denomination as listed.
unpack.consequence: Connect the physical thread with what is written on it.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom into the thread and its lettering.
unpack.level_extra: A printed line alone is not equivalent to the security thread.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the recognition cue for the latent image?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says the image becomes visible when the note is tilted.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the user look for it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The user examines the designated latent-image area on the note while changing the viewing angle.

teacher_understanding.question: How is this different from a normal printed image?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its visibility depends on viewing angle, whereas ordinary print is generally readable without seeking that angle.

p009-i17.exam_note: Match latent image with tilting, not with a magnifying glass.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा छिपा चित्र जो खास angle से दिखे
terms.everyday_image: note झुकाते ही पहले छिपा निशान उभरना

why_chain.step: A flat copy may reproduce a visible design.
Angle-dependent visibility supplies a different checking action.

unpack.example_or_place: The latent-image feature on a note.
unpack.consequence: Teach tilt as a distinct action from holding against light.
unpack.visual_verb: Tilt the note until the image appears.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse image appearance with colour-changing ink.

p009-i18.content: See-through Register that forms the denomination when viewed against light.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the see-through register form?
teacher_understanding.answer: It forms the denomination when viewed against light.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the complementary parts located?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parts of the design are printed in matching positions on the front and back of the note.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the complete number become visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: Transmitted light lets the viewer see the front and back portions together, so correctly aligned parts complete the numeral.

prerequisites: front and reverse of a note
p009-i18.exam_note: Match the register with front–back alignment against light.

terms.plain_meaning: आगे-पीछे छपे हिस्से जो रोशनी में मिलकर पूरा अंक बनाएँ
terms.everyday_image: दो अधूरे हिस्से मिलकर पूरा number बनाना

why_chain.step: A convincing note needs accurate printing on both sides.
The register tests whether the two parts align into the denomination.

unpack.example_or_place: The denomination completed when a note is held against light.
unpack.consequence: Distinguishes alignment checking from watermark recognition.
unpack.visual_verb: Overlay front and back fragments into one numeral.
unpack.level_extra: Watermark and register use light but are different features.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the micro-lettering read?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies the tiny lettering as “RBI” and the denomination.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is micro-lettering examined?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is examined in the small-print security areas of the note, rather than in the large value numerals.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it help authentication?
teacher_understanding.answer: Magnification can reveal whether the tiny lettering is formed clearly; ordinary copying may blur such fine detail.

p009-i19.exam_note: Link micro-lettering with tiny readable detail.

terms.plain_meaning: बहुत छोटे आकार में लिखे अक्षर और अंक
terms.everyday_image: magnifying glass से छोटे RBI अक्षर पढ़ना

why_chain.step: A counterfeit may reproduce large shapes but lose fine detail.
Tiny lettering adds a detail that can be checked closely.

unpack.example_or_place: “RBI” and denomination in the listed micro-lettering.
unpack.consequence: Adds a close-inspection check to light and tilt checks.
unpack.visual_verb: Magnify tiny print into readable letters.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse micro-lettering with larger accessibility numerals.

p009-i20.content: Optically Variable Ink on higher denominations.

teacher_understanding.question: What feature is listed for higher denominations?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page lists Optically Variable Ink.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the page place this feature?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates the ink with higher-denomination notes without specifying particular values.

teacher_understanding.question: How does optically variable ink behave?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its apparent colour changes with viewing angle, supplying a visual check that ordinary single-colour printing does not provide.

p009-i20.exam_note: The page limits the claim to higher denominations; do not universalise it.

terms.plain_meaning: angle बदलने पर अलग रंग दिखाने वाली ink
terms.everyday_image: note झुकाते समय छपे हिस्से का रंग बदलता दिखना

why_chain.step: A static colour copy can imitate ordinary printing.
Angle-dependent colour adds a changing visual cue.

unpack.example_or_place: Higher denominations as stated on the page.
unpack.consequence: Tilt can test colour change as well as latent-image visibility.
unpack.visual_verb: Tilt and change the ink's apparent colour.
unpack.level_extra: Colour change and latent-image appearance are separate mechanisms.

p009-i21.content: Intaglio Printing (raised printing) for tactile feel.

teacher_understanding.question: What does intaglio printing provide here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes it as raised printing that gives a tactile feel.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the effect felt?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is felt on the raised printed portions of the note surface.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this link security with accessibility?
teacher_understanding.answer: A user can feel relief rather than rely only on sight, providing a physical recognition cue that also assists users with impaired vision.

prerequisites: touch as a way of recognition
p009-i21.exam_note: Associate intaglio with raised tactile printing.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी printing जिससे छपा हिस्सा उभरा महसूस हो
terms.everyday_image: उँगली फेरने पर चिकने paper से अलग उभार महसूस करना

why_chain.step: Visual inspection alone is not equally useful to all users.
Raised printing supplies a tactile recognition cue.

unpack.example_or_place: Raised printed portions of a note.
unpack.consequence: Connects the security list back to accessibility features.
unpack.visual_verb: Run a fingertip across raised print.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid treating a flat printed imitation of a raised mark as equivalent.

p009-i22.content: Number Panels with increasing numeral size.

teacher_understanding.question: What pattern does the page identify in number panels?
teacher_understanding.answer: The numerals increase in size within the number panels.

teacher_understanding.question: Where should this pattern be checked?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is checked in the note's numbering panels, not by comparing the large denomination numerals on different notes.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from a rise in monetary value?
teacher_understanding.answer: The change is in printed character size; it does not change the face value of the note.

p009-i22.exam_note: Increasing numeral size is not increasing denomination.

terms.plain_meaning: note पर उसका पहचान number छपा हुआ हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: एक line में छोटे से बड़े होते छपे अंक

why_chain.step: Users need recognisable printing details to compare with an expected design.
The page supplies increasing numeral size as one such pattern.

unpack.example_or_place: Numbering panels on the note.
unpack.consequence: Completes the page's multi-feature security checklist.
unpack.visual_verb: Enlarge consecutive numerals along the panel.
unpack.level_extra: Keep serial numbering separate from denomination.

p009-i24.where_on_page: first bullet under Promise on the Note
p009-i24.content: It is known as the Promise Clause, and it signifies that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guarantees the face value of the note.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the promise clause signify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It signifies RBI's guarantee of the amount written as the note's face value.

teacher_understanding.question: Which kind of value is explicitly guaranteed on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page specifies face value, rather than an inflation-adjusted value or a weight of precious metal.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is face value different from purchasing power?
teacher_understanding.answer: A ₹100 note remains denominated at ₹100 even if rising prices mean that ₹100 buys fewer goods.

p009-i24.exam_note: Nominal guarantee is not an inflation-protection or gold-redemption guarantee.

terms.plain_meaning: note पर लिखी रकम की RBI की guarantee बताने वाली बात
terms.everyday_image: note पर छपी ‘I PROMISE TO PAY’ वाली line

terms.plain_meaning: note पर लिखी रुपये की रकम
terms.everyday_image: ₹100 लिखा है तो उसकी face value ₹100

why_chain.step: A user needs confidence in the amount the note represents.
The page explains the promise as RBI's guarantee of face value.

unpack.example_or_place: The promise text shown in the note photograph.
unpack.consequence: Sets up the distinction between nominal money and metal or purchasing-power claims.
unpack.visual_verb: Underline the promise and connect it to the printed amount.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer the legal status of a promissory note merely from the word promise.

p009-i25.content: Bearer means that whoever physically possesses the note can use it.

teacher_understanding.question: Who is the bearer in this explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The bearer is the person physically holding the note and able to use it in payment.

teacher_understanding.question: What criterion identifies the bearer on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The criterion is physical possession, not a payee's name written on the note.

teacher_understanding.question: How does bearer use differ from a named bank account?
teacher_understanding.answer: A note can pass from hand to hand without changing a named account holder in bank records; an account balance is maintained against an identified account.

p009-i25.exam_note: Physical possession explains bearer use, not lawful ownership in every possible circumstance.

terms.plain_meaning: वह व्यक्ति जिसके हाथ में note है
terms.everyday_image: ग्राहक note दुकानदार को देता है और अब दुकानदार उसे आगे खर्च करता है

why_chain.step: Cash must pass between people without rewriting a payee's name.
Bearer use lets the physical holder use the note.

unpack.example_or_place: A note handed over at a shop.
unpack.consequence: Helps explain the later description of cash as anonymous.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass the note between hands.
unpack.level_extra: Possession and legal title should not be conflated.

p009-i26.content: Colonial era: Promised to convert into full bodied gold or silver bars / coins worth the equal value in weight.

teacher_understanding.question: To which period does the page attach metal convertibility?
teacher_understanding.answer: It attaches the promise of conversion into full-bodied gold or silver bars or coins to the colonial era.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does metal convertibility change the meaning of the promise?
teacher_understanding.answer: Under a convertible arrangement, the holder's claim is linked to specified metal redemption rather than simply the continued acceptance of a nominal currency amount.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the broad historical statement be handled carefully?
teacher_understanding.answer: Convertibility depended on the monetary system, period and eligible holder. This line should not be expanded into a claim that every colonial note was freely redeemable into either metal throughout colonial rule.

p009-i26.exam_note: Use the intended contrast with modern fiat currency, but avoid universal historical claims.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसमें metal की अपनी कीमत बताए गए मूल्य के बराबर हो
terms.everyday_image: ऐसा gold coin जिसकी कीमत उसके gold से आती हो

why_chain.step: People may seek a tangible asset behind a paper claim.
The page describes a historical promise to convert notes into gold or silver.

unpack.example_or_place: The page's colonial-era description of bars and coins.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the contrast with modern currency unlinked to metal weight.
unpack.visual_verb: Exchange a paper note for a metal bar or coin.
unpack.level_extra: Separate the book's broad contrast from precise period-specific convertibility rules.

p009-i27.content: Same was with the Dollar during the Bretton Woods System and the Pound Sterling during the British Rule.

teacher_understanding.question: Which historical settings does the page use as parallels?
teacher_understanding.answer: It names the Dollar during the Bretton Woods System and Pound Sterling during British Rule as parallels to metal-linked currency.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the book bring these currencies into the discussion?
teacher_understanding.answer: They illustrate its contrast between earlier metal-linked promises and modern currency not tied to a metal weight.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the Bretton Woods example be qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dollar–gold convertibility under Bretton Woods was available to foreign official monetary holders, not a general right of every retail dollar holder. It therefore does not imply unrestricted public redemption of notes.

p009-i27.exam_note: Bretton Woods is an important linkage; avoid equating official convertibility with universal bearer redemption.

terms.plain_meaning: पुराना अंतरराष्ट्रीय money system जिसमें Dollar का gold से तय रिश्ता था
terms.everyday_image: अलग देशों के money system को Dollar के जरिए जोड़ती chain

why_chain.step: The historical contrast needs recognisable examples.
The page supplies the Dollar and Pound Sterling as parallels.

unpack.example_or_place: Dollar under Bretton Woods; Pound Sterling during British Rule.
unpack.consequence: Connects domestic currency promises with international monetary arrangements.
unpack.visual_verb: Place the two currencies on historical tracks beside metal.
unpack.level_extra: The page gives no precise dates or sterling redemption conditions.

p009-i28.content: Close-up of an Indian note showing a Hindi promise at left, the English words “I PROMISE TO PAY THE BEARER THE SUM OF … HUNDRED RUPEES” at right, and a signature with “GOVERNOR” below. The amount is partly obscured. Hindi text includes “मैं धारक को … रुपये अदा करने का वचन देता हूँ” and the guarantee wording “केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा प्रत्याभूत” below; part of the denomination is obscured.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the photograph demonstrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows the promise wording and Governor's signature area on a physical note.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible wording connects it to the definitions above?
teacher_understanding.answer: “I PROMISE TO PAY THE BEARER” connects the image to both the promise clause and bearer.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the image be used without overreading it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use the legible promise and role label as evidence; do not infer a precise denomination from the obscured amount.

p009-i28.exam_note: The Governor label in this illustration must not override the ₹1 note's Finance Secretary exception.

unpack.example_or_place: Printed banknote close-up beside the historical discussion.
unpack.consequence: Anchors the abstract definitions in visible note wording.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom into promise, bearer and signature.
unpack.level_extra: Read only legible text; distinguish this photograph from the ₹1-note facts.

p009-i29.content: Hindi promise and English “I PROMISE TO PAY THE BEARER THE SUM OF … HUNDRED RUPEES”: the printed payment promise, with the amount partly obscured.

teacher_understanding.question: What do these lines label?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are the promise printed on the illustrated note, in Hindi and English.

teacher_understanding.question: Which English word identifies the person addressed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The promise addresses the “BEARER”.

teacher_understanding.question: How does that wording connect to possession?
teacher_understanding.answer: It addresses the holder rather than naming a particular individual as payee.

p009-i29.exam_note: Recognise promise wording without inferring metal redemption.

unpack.example_or_place: Promise lines in the banknote photograph.
unpack.consequence: Visual evidence for the promise-clause definition.
unpack.visual_verb: Underline “PROMISE” and “BEARER”.

p009-i30.content: “केन्द्रीय सरकार द्वारा प्रत्याभूत”: the Hindi guarantee wording below the promise area.

teacher_understanding.question: What additional wording appears in the image?
teacher_understanding.answer: The image includes Hindi wording stating a Central Government guarantee.

teacher_understanding.question: Which area of the image contains it?
teacher_understanding.answer: It appears below the Hindi promise, toward the lower left of the cropped note.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this be distinguished from the promise clause?
teacher_understanding.answer: The guarantee wording and the Governor's payment promise are related but separate printed elements; their presence should not be collapsed into one quotation.

p009-i30.exam_note: Keep the guarantee wording distinct from issuer and signatory facts.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसकी guarantee दी गई है
terms.everyday_image: लिखी रकम के पीछे guarantee का भरोसा

unpack.example_or_place: Lower-left wording in the photographed note.
unpack.consequence: Adds a visible institutional assurance beyond the promise text.
unpack.visual_verb: Highlight the separate guarantee line.

p009-i31.content: Signature above “GOVERNOR”: identifies the signatory's office on the illustrated note.

teacher_understanding.question: What office is identified below the signature?
teacher_understanding.answer: The visible label reads “GOVERNOR”.

teacher_understanding.question: Which separately discussed note has a different signatory?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page specifies the Finance Secretary of India as the signatory of the ₹1 note.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner reconcile the image and the ₹1 bullet?
teacher_understanding.answer: The photograph illustrates a Governor-signed note; it does not mean that the ₹1 note carries the same signature.

p009-i31.exam_note: Do not generalise the pictured signature to ₹1 notes.

unpack.example_or_place: Signature and GOVERNOR label in the inset.
unpack.consequence: Reinforces the need to distinguish note categories.
unpack.visual_verb: Circle GOVERNOR and contrast it with Finance Secretary.

p009-i33.content: Not inflation adjusted value. Not linked with weight of gold or silver.

teacher_understanding.question: How does modern currency differ from the earlier metal-linked description?
teacher_understanding.answer: The earlier description promises conversion into gold or silver; modern currency is described as not linked to a weight of either metal.

teacher_understanding.question: How is nominal face value different from inflation-adjusted value?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nominal value is the printed rupee amount. Inflation-adjusted value accounts for how much goods and services that amount can buy as prices change.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a face-value guarantee not protect purchasing power?
teacher_understanding.answer: It preserves the stated monetary amount, not the prices of goods. If prices rise, the same amount buys less.

teacher_understanding.question: What two protections does the page say modern currency does not provide?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is not inflation adjusted and is not linked to a weight of gold or silver.

p009-i33.exam_note: Distinguish nominal value, real purchasing power and metal redemption.

terms.plain_meaning: महँगाई बदलने पर खरीदने की ताकत के हिसाब से बदली रकम
terms.everyday_image: पहले ₹100 में भरी थैली अब उसी ₹100 में आधी भरना

why_chain.step: Users care about both the rupee amount and what it buys.
The page limits modern currency's promise: no inflation adjustment and no gold or silver weight link.

unpack.example_or_place: A ₹100 note whose printed value stays ₹100 while shopping prices change.
unpack.consequence: Trust in currency does not imply a fixed real value.
unpack.visual_verb: Keep ₹100 fixed while the goods basket shrinks; disconnect a gold-weight link.
unpack.level_extra: No metal-redemption link does not mean that an issuing institution holds no gold assets.

p009-i34.content: Currency note is zero interest, anonymous bearer bond.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three attributes does the book attach to the note?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes a currency note as zero interest, anonymous and bearer, using the expression “bearer bond”.

teacher_understanding.question: Which earlier definition supports the bearer attribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page has already defined bearer as the person who physically possesses the note and can use it.

teacher_understanding.question: How should zero interest and anonymous be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Holding a cash note does not itself earn interest, and the note is not registered in the holder's name. This does not mean that every cash transaction is untraceable.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the word bond be treated cautiously?
teacher_understanding.answer: Here it is an economic shorthand for an issuer-backed bearer claim, not a reason to classify ordinary currency as a conventional investment bond with maturity and redemption terms.

p009-i34.exam_note: Open each adjective separately; do not infer legal promissory-note or conventional bond status.

terms.plain_meaning: note अपने पास रखने भर से ब्याज नहीं मिलता
terms.everyday_image: जेब का ₹100 note अगले महीने भी ₹100 ही रहता है

terms.plain_meaning: note पर उसे रखने वाले व्यक्ति का नाम दर्ज नहीं होता
terms.everyday_image: एक ही note अलग हाथों में जाता है, उस पर नाम नहीं बदलता

terms.plain_meaning: यहाँ ऐसा दावा समझाने का तरीका जिसे note रखने वाला इस्तेमाल करे
terms.everyday_image: note हाथ बदलता है तो उसे खर्च करने वाला भी बदलता है

why_chain.step: Cash is designed for ready transfer rather than interest income.
The book groups its non-interest-bearing, unnamed-holder and bearer features in one description.

unpack.example_or_place: A cash note held in a wallet and later handed to a seller.
unpack.consequence: Links the bearer definition to modern money while requiring care with financial and legal labels.
unpack.visual_verb: Pass an unnamed note between hands while its amount stays unchanged.
unpack.level_extra: Economic description and legal classification are not interchangeable.

p010-i1.content: An Indian currency note is not a promissory note in the legal sense, even though it contains a promise clause.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a currency note compare with a legal promissory note?
teacher_understanding.answer: A promise clause appears on the currency note, but the page says this does not make it a promissory note in law.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the decisive legal distinction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The quoted Section 4 definition expressly excludes bank-notes and currency-notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the presence of a promise insufficient?
teacher_understanding.answer: Legal categories depend on the statutory definition, not simply on similar wording on two documents.

p010-i1.exam_note: Trap: a promise clause does not establish legal classification as a promissory note.

terms.plain_meaning: नोट पर भुगतान का वादा लिखने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: किसी कागज़ पर पैसे लौटाने का वादा लिखा होना

why_chain.step: Similar wording can make two documents look legally identical.
Section 4 excludes currency-notes, so wording alone cannot decide their category.

unpack.example_or_place: The promise printed on an Indian currency note.
unpack.consequence: Read the statutory exclusion before classifying the instrument.
unpack.visual_verb: separate
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish everyday meaning from legal meaning.

p010-i2.content: Section 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881: A promissory note is: ”An instrument in writing (not being a bank-note or a currency-note) containing an unconditional undertaking.
p010-i2.type_note: The year identifies the statute; the content defines a legal instrument rather than narrating events.

teacher_understanding.question: What elements of the definition are quoted?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a written instrument containing an unconditional undertaking, with bank-notes and currency-notes expressly excluded.

teacher_understanding.question: Which provision supports the exclusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page cites Section 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, especially the words 'not being a bank-note or a currency-note'.

teacher_understanding.question: How should unconditional undertaking be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It means a definite commitment not dependent on an uncertain condition, unlike 'I will pay if my business succeeds'.

p010-i2.exam_note: Remember Section 4 and the express exclusion; this is only the extract printed here.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा पक्का वादा जिसके साथ कोई 'अगर' नहीं लगा है
terms.everyday_image: 'पैसे दूँगा' और 'नौकरी मिली तो पैसे दूँगा' में फर्क

why_chain.step: A payment commitment needs a clear legal meaning.
The quoted definition specifies writing and an unconditional undertaking while excluding currency-notes.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare an unconditional written payment promise with a currency note.
unpack.consequence: The statutory exception resolves the apparent contradiction in i1.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight
unpack.level_extra: Do not present this incomplete quotation as the whole statutory definition.

p010-i4.content: MANI (Mobile Aided Note Identifier): It is a free mobile app launched by the Reserve Bank of India on 1 January 2020.

teacher_understanding.question: When and by whom was MANI launched?
teacher_understanding.answer: The Reserve Bank of India launched the free Mobile Aided Note Identifier app on 1 January 2020.

teacher_understanding.question: Why was the app introduced?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its stated purpose is to help visually impaired persons independently identify Indian banknote denominations.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a free mobile tool support this purpose?
teacher_understanding.answer: It can reduce dependence on another person for reading a note’s value without charging an app purchase price.

p010-i4.exam_note: Know expansion, RBI, free access and launch date.

terms.plain_meaning: फोन की मदद से नोट की कीमत पहचानने वाला app
terms.everyday_image: फोन नोट देखकर उसकी रकम बताता है

why_chain.step: Reading a printed denomination can be difficult for someone with impaired vision.
RBI launched a free identification app for independent use.

unpack.example_or_place: Identifying money received as change.
unpack.consequence: Links RBI’s currency role with accessibility.
unpack.visual_verb: launch
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse the developer institution with a commercial bank.

p010-i5.content: To help visually impaired persons identify the denomination of Indian banknotes independently.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is independent denomination identification important?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reading printed values may be difficult for visually impaired users; independent identification reduces the need to ask another person.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page show MANI helping these users?
teacher_understanding.answer: The graphic shows scanning either side of a banknote and providing denomination information through audio, with vibration for users with vision and hearing impairment.

p010-i5.exam_note: Purpose is denomination identification; the page does not establish counterfeit authentication.

terms.plain_meaning: नोट पर लिखी रकम, जैसे ₹100 या ₹500
terms.everyday_image: दुकान पर ₹100 और ₹500 का नोट अलग करना

why_chain.step: A user needs to know the value of money being received or paid.
MANI helps visually impaired persons identify that value independently.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking a banknote before paying a shopkeeper.
unpack.consequence: Accessibility supports independent transactions.
unpack.visual_verb: identify
unpack.level_extra: Keep denomination recognition distinct from genuineness testing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which mobile platforms does MANI support?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page lists both Android and iOS rather than restricting access to one platform.

teacher_understanding.question: What wording supports cross-platform availability?
teacher_understanding.answer: The explicit bullet says 'Android and iOS both.'

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this matter for accessibility?
teacher_understanding.answer: People using either major phone platform can use the tool without changing platforms for this purpose.

p010-i6.exam_note: Reject a statement limiting MANI to Android alone.

terms.plain_meaning: फोन चलाने वाले दो अलग software platform
terms.everyday_image: Android फोन और iPhone

why_chain.step: Users own different types of smartphones.
Support for both platforms broadens access.

unpack.example_or_place: Android phones and iPhones.
unpack.consequence: Platform choice is not restricted to one of these two systems.
unpack.visual_verb: pair
unpack.level_extra: A simple statement-combination fact.

p010-i7.type_note: This is an operating capability, not a sequence of process stages.

teacher_understanding.question: What connectivity feature is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Once installed, MANI can work offline.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is this feature confirmed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both the bullet and the graphic explicitly say it works offline after installation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is offline operation useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Denomination identification need not depend on an active internet connection at the time of use.

terms.plain_meaning: उस समय internet जुड़े बिना काम करना
terms.everyday_image: फोन में पहले से रखी फोटो बिना data के खोलना

why_chain.step: A user may need to identify cash where connectivity is poor.
Offline operation after installation removes that immediate connectivity dependence.

unpack.example_or_place: A shop with weak mobile data coverage.
unpack.consequence: Do not interpret offline operation as requiring no initial installation.
unpack.visual_verb: disconnect
unpack.level_extra: The qualifying words 'after installation' matter.

p010-i8.content: Supports 15 Languages, including Hindi and English

teacher_understanding.question: What language support is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page reports 15 languages and names Hindi and English among them.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page list all 15 languages?
teacher_understanding.answer: No; only Hindi and English are named, so the remaining languages cannot be enumerated from this page.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does multilingual support matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: An audio-based accessibility tool is more usable when the user understands the language of its output.

p010-i8.exam_note: Retain the page’s count without inventing the remaining language names.

terms.plain_meaning: app में 15 भाषाओं का सहारा मिलता है
terms.everyday_image: फोन में अपनी समझ की भाषा चुनना

why_chain.step: Users may not understand the same language.
Multiple language options make the tool usable for more people.

unpack.example_or_place: Hindi or English language use.
unpack.consequence: Accessibility includes language as well as sensory access.
unpack.visual_verb: switch
unpack.level_extra: Treat this as the book’s stated feature count.

p010-i9.content: Four feature panels in a two-by-two layout: camera icon—scans front or back of Indian banknotes; speaker icon—audio output for denomination; vibrating-phone icon—vibration for users with vision and hearing impairment; crossed wireless icon—offline operation after installation. No arrows or sequence are shown.
p010-i9.exam_note: Children capture the four feature labels.

p010-i10.content: Scans front or back of Indian banknotes.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the camera panel show?
teacher_understanding.answer: The note can be scanned from its front or its back.

teacher_understanding.question: Which face must be used?
teacher_understanding.answer: The label permits either face rather than specifying just one.

teacher_understanding.question: How does scanning support identification?
teacher_understanding.answer: A camera supplies an image from which the app can recognise the denomination.

p010-i10.exam_note: Front-only scanning would misstate the graphic.

terms.plain_meaning: camera से नोट की तस्वीर पढ़ता है
terms.everyday_image: फोन का camera किसी कागज़ की ओर करना

why_chain.step: The app needs visual information about the banknote.
Either side supplies an accepted scan according to the graphic.

unpack.example_or_place: Pointing the phone camera at a banknote.
unpack.consequence: Scanning is the input side of the identification function.
unpack.visual_verb: scan
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer authenticity certification from scanning.

teacher_understanding.question: What information is delivered through audio?
teacher_understanding.answer: The output communicates the banknote’s denomination.

teacher_understanding.question: Which icon represents this feature?
teacher_understanding.answer: The speaker icon marks the audio-output panel.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use sound rather than only on-screen text?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sound allows a user who cannot easily read the screen to receive the note’s value.

p010-i11.exam_note: Connect the output mode to MANI’s accessibility purpose.

terms.plain_meaning: जानकारी आवाज़ में सुनाई देना
terms.everyday_image: फोन रकम बोलकर सुनाए

why_chain.step: A visual display may be difficult for the intended user to read.
Audio makes denomination information available through hearing.

unpack.example_or_place: Hearing a note’s value from a phone.
unpack.consequence: The user need not rely solely on sight.
unpack.visual_verb: announce
unpack.level_extra: Input is visual scanning; output can be audible.

p010-i12.content: Uses vibration for users with vision and hearing impairment.

teacher_understanding.question: What additional accessible output does the graphic identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies vibration for users with both vision and hearing impairment.

teacher_understanding.question: Which users are specifically associated with vibration?
teacher_understanding.answer: The panel explicitly mentions users with vision and hearing impairment.

teacher_understanding.question: Why add vibration when audio already exists?
teacher_understanding.answer: Audio may not be accessible to a person with hearing impairment; vibration provides a touch-based signal.

p010-i12.exam_note: Image-only accessibility detail; do not omit dual sensory impairment.

terms.plain_meaning: फोन का कंपन, जिसे हाथ से महसूस कर सकें
terms.everyday_image: silent mode में फोन का हाथ में हिलना

why_chain.step: Some users cannot readily use sight or hearing for feedback.
Vibration offers a touch-based route for feedback.

unpack.example_or_place: A vibrating phone held in the hand.
unpack.consequence: Accessibility is not limited to spoken output.
unpack.visual_verb: vibrate
unpack.level_extra: The page does not specify a vibration code; do not invent one.

p010-i13.where_on_page: feature graphic, bottom-right crossed wireless panel

teacher_understanding.question: What does the crossed wireless panel communicate?
teacher_understanding.answer: MANI works without an active internet connection after installation.

teacher_understanding.question: Which qualification accompanies offline use?
teacher_understanding.answer: The app must already have been installed.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this useful in daily transactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: A user may need to identify cash even where mobile connectivity is unavailable.

why_chain.step: Cash identification may be needed without internet access.
The graphic confirms offline use after installation.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking cash in a low-connectivity location.
unpack.consequence: Connectivity loss need not prevent use.
unpack.visual_verb: disconnect
unpack.level_extra: Same feature as i7, captured separately to preserve the graphic.

p010-i15.content: Demonetization means the REMOVAL of legal tender status of currency notes. It becomes invalid for transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: What changes in demonetisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The note loses its legal-tender status; the page describes it as becoming invalid for transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words define the decisive test?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page emphasises 'REMOVAL of legal tender status', not merely stopping printing or withdrawing notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is legal-tender status more important than physical possession?
teacher_understanding.answer: A person can still hold the paper note after its legal payment status changes; the policy changes its legal role, not its physical existence.

p010-i15.exam_note: Core definition distinguishes demonetisation from withdrawal.

terms.plain_meaning: पैसे के रूप में भुगतान के लिए कानून से मिली मान्यता
terms.everyday_image: हाथ में रखा नोट और उसे भुगतान में मान्यता मिलना दो अलग बातें

why_chain.step: A currency policy can change a note’s legal payment status.
Removal of that status is what the page calls demonetisation.

unpack.example_or_place: Existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes in the 2016 announcement.
unpack.consequence: Use legal status, not disappearance from circulation, as the test.
unpack.visual_verb: remove
unpack.level_extra: Avoid assuming that every withdrawn note is demonetised.

p010-i16.content: India has carried out three major demonetisations—in 1946, 1978, and 2016.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three years does the book identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It lists 1946, 1978 and 2016 as India’s three major demonetisations.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 2023 not a fourth event in this list?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says the ₹2,000 notes withdrawn in 2023 remained legal tender.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the chronology be retained without confusing events?
teacher_understanding.answer: Attach each year to its government and affected denominations using the adjacent table, rather than memorising four years as equivalent events.

p010-i16.exam_note: Chronology and the exclusion of 2023 are statement-combination targets.

why_chain.step: Different currency events can be confused when only years are memorised.
Classify by legal-tender removal, keeping 2023 outside the three major demonetisations.

unpack.consequence: The table adds the denomination and government associations.
unpack.visual_verb: sequence
unpack.level_extra: Keep pre-independence 1946 distinct from the later two events.

p010-i17.content: 8 November 2016: PM Modi announced that existing: ₹500 notes and ₹1,000 notes would cease to be legal tender from midnight.

teacher_understanding.question: When was the announcement made and when did the stated change take effect?
teacher_understanding.answer: PM Modi announced it on 8 November 2016, with the existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes ceasing to be legal tender from midnight.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this event qualify as demonetisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The existing notes lost legal-tender status, which is the page’s defining criterion.

teacher_understanding.question: Which wording prevents overgeneralisation to every ₹500 note?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page specifies 'existing' notes in that announcement.

p010-i17.exam_note: Distinguish announcement date, midnight effect and affected existing notes.

terms.plain_meaning: भुगतान के पैसे के रूप में कानूनी मान्यता खत्म होना
terms.everyday_image: रात के समय एक नोट की कानूनी स्थिति बदलने की समयरेखा

why_chain.step: A legal currency change needs an effective time and specified notes.
The announcement names existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes and midnight.

unpack.example_or_place: 8 November 2016 announcement.
unpack.consequence: Introduces the need for replacement currency discussed below.
unpack.visual_verb: switch
unpack.level_extra: Do not add unstated policy objectives to this page’s account.

p010-i18.content: A withdrawal of ₹2,000 notes in 2023, which was not a demonetisation because the notes remained legal tender.
p010-i18.type_note: The combined sentence explains classification through retained legal-tender status; the year is contextual.

teacher_understanding.question: Why was the 2023 ₹2,000 withdrawal not demonetisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The notes retained legal-tender status, so the defining removal of that status did not occur.

teacher_understanding.question: How should withdrawal and demonetisation be distinguished?
teacher_understanding.answer: Withdrawal concerns taking notes out of circulation; demonetisation concerns removing their legal-tender status. These need not coincide.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the page contrast 2016 and 2023?
teacher_understanding.answer: The affected existing notes in 2016 ceased to be legal tender, whereas the withdrawn ₹2,000 notes in 2023 remained legal tender.

p010-i18.exam_note: Central trap: withdrawal does not necessarily mean demonetisation.

terms.plain_meaning: नोट को चलन से वापस लेने की कार्रवाई
terms.everyday_image: नोट बैंक में लौट रहा है, लेकिन उसकी legal tender मान्यता अलग सवाल है

why_chain.step: A note can be taken out of circulation without cancelling its legal status.
The page says ₹2,000 notes retained legal-tender status in the 2023 withdrawal.

unpack.example_or_place: 2023 withdrawal of ₹2,000 notes.
unpack.consequence: 2023 must not be counted with the three demonetisations.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast
unpack.level_extra: Test two separate propositions: circulation action and legal status.

p010-i19.content: 2016-Nov: RBI introduced ₹2000 note, to meet the currency requirement of the economy in an [a] faster manner after demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1000

teacher_understanding.question: When did RBI introduce the ₹2,000 note?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page places its introduction in November 2016, following demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why was the note introduced according to this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: It was introduced to meet the economy’s currency requirement more quickly.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a larger denomination help supply a given value of cash?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fewer individual notes are needed: ₹2,000 of value requires one ₹2,000 note but four ₹500 notes.

p010-i19.exam_note: Link introduction date to the stated replacement-currency need.

terms.plain_meaning: लेन-देन के लिए अर्थव्यवस्था को जितनी नकदी चाहिए
terms.everyday_image: दुकान, ग्राहक और मजदूरी देने के लिए नकदी चाहिए

why_chain.step: After demonetisation, the economy needed replacement currency.
A higher denomination supplies a given cash value through fewer pieces of paper.

unpack.example_or_place: One ₹2,000 note compared with four ₹500 notes.
unpack.consequence: Introduces the first stage of the ₹2,000 note’s later printing and withdrawal timeline.
unpack.visual_verb: replace
unpack.level_extra: The arithmetic explains the stated rationale; it is not an additional quoted policy claim.

teacher_understanding.question: When does the page say printing stopped?
teacher_understanding.answer: It gives 2018–19 for stopping the printing of ₹2,000 banknotes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should stopping printing not be read as demonetisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stopping new production does not itself remove legal-tender status from notes already issued.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this event fit the chronology?
teacher_understanding.answer: It follows the November 2016 introduction and precedes the 2023 withdrawal described on the page.

p010-i20.exam_note: Do not equate cessation of printing with withdrawal or demonetisation.

terms.plain_meaning: नए नोट बनाना
terms.everyday_image: नई प्रतियाँ छापना बंद हो, फिर भी पुरानी प्रतियाँ मौजूद रहती हैं

why_chain.step: Students can confuse making new notes with the status of existing notes.
A printing stop concerns fresh supply, not automatic cancellation of existing notes.

unpack.example_or_place: ₹2,000 note printing in 2018–19.
unpack.consequence: Keep production, circulation and legal status as separate dimensions.
unpack.visual_verb: stop
unpack.level_extra: The page does not give a reason for stopping printing.

p010-i21.content: 2023-May-23rd: RBI ordered people to get it exchanged with other notes.

teacher_understanding.question: What date and instruction does the book print?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page prints '2023-May-23rd' and says RBI ordered people to exchange the note with other notes.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the correct distinction between the announcement and exchange dates?
teacher_understanding.answer: RBI announced withdrawal of ₹2,000 notes on 19 May 2023. Exchange at bank branches began on 23 May 2023. The printed sentence misleadingly associates the latter date with an order to exchange.

teacher_understanding.question: What options did holders have, and was everyone ordered to exchange notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Holders could deposit the notes into bank accounts or exchange them. This was not an order requiring everyone to exchange them for other notes, and the notes remained legal tender.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page distinguish this withdrawal from demonetisation?
teacher_understanding.answer: The accompanying text explicitly says the ₹2,000 notes remained legal tender; their legal-tender status was not removed.

p010-i21.exam_note: Printed wording is misleading: withdrawal announced 19 May 2023; branch exchange began 23 May. Deposit and exchange were options; legal-tender status continued.

terms.plain_meaning: एक नोट देकर उतनी ही रकम के दूसरे नोट लेना
नोट बैंक खाते में जमा करके उतनी रकम खाते में जुड़वाना
terms.everyday_image: नकदी बैंक को देना और खाते का balance बढ़ना

why_chain.step: Withdrawal needs arrangements for holders to return notes without confusing return with cancellation of legal status.
Holders could deposit or exchange ₹2,000 notes; branch exchange began on 23 May after the 19 May announcement, and the notes remained legal tender.

unpack.example_or_place: A bank branch: deposit credits an account; exchange supplies equal-value notes.
unpack.consequence: Do not mistake the start of exchange for the withdrawal announcement, or treat exchange as the sole compulsory option.
unpack.visual_verb: split dates and branch into deposit or exchange
unpack.level_extra: Outside correction: 19 May = withdrawal announcement; 23 May = branch exchange commencement. Preserve the printed claim but do not teach its 'ordered people' wording as accurate.

p010-i22.content: Columns: Year | Government | Currency affected. Four rows compare 1946, 1978, 2016 and 2023; the last is explicitly withdrawal, not demonetisation.
p010-i22.exam_note: Read every row with all three columns.

p010-i23.content: Year: 1946 | Government: British India | Currency affected: ₹500, ₹1,000, ₹10,000

teacher_understanding.question: Which event belongs to British India?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates the 1946 event with British India and the ₹500, ₹1,000 and ₹10,000 denominations.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the government label important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It locates this currency action before independence, preventing confusion with governments of independent India.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its denomination list differ from 1978?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both lists include ₹1,000 and ₹10,000; 1946 lists ₹500, whereas 1978 lists ₹5,000.

p010-i23.exam_note: Match year, government and all three denominations.

why_chain.step: Repeated denominations across events make year-matching difficult.
Attach the 1946 set to British India as one memory unit.

unpack.consequence: Creates a contrast with the 1978 set.
unpack.visual_verb: align
unpack.level_extra: ₹500 versus ₹5,000 is the key contrast with 1978.

p010-i24.content: Year: 1978 | Government: Morarji Desai | Currency affected: ₹1,000, ₹5,000, ₹10,000

teacher_understanding.question: Which event does the table associate with Morarji Desai?
teacher_understanding.answer: The 1978 event affected ₹1,000, ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should this row not be merged with 2016?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table gives different governments and different sets: 1978 includes ₹5,000 and ₹10,000, while 2016 lists ₹500 and ₹1,000.

teacher_understanding.question: How can the denomination set be remembered?
teacher_understanding.answer: Associate 1978 with the three listed high denominations, 1,000–5,000–10,000, rather than borrowing the familiar 2016 pair.

p010-i24.exam_note: Common matching trap: substitute the 2016 denominations for the 1978 set.

why_chain.step: The familiar 2016 pair can overshadow earlier denomination sets.
Link Morarji Desai and 1978 directly to 1,000–5,000–10,000.

unpack.example_or_place: 1978 row of the table.
unpack.consequence: Supports accurate matching questions.
unpack.visual_verb: group
unpack.level_extra: The page does not explain the policy motive for 1978.

p010-i25.content: Year: 2016 | Government: Narendra Modi | Currency affected: ₹500, ₹1,000

teacher_understanding.question: Which denomination pair belongs to 2016?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates Narendra Modi’s government in 2016 with ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is ₹2,000 not an affected denomination in this row?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page describes ₹2,000 as introduced after the demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1,000, rather than demonetised in that event.

p010-i25.exam_note: Separate affected notes from the subsequently introduced ₹2,000 note.

why_chain.step: Notes removed and notes introduced can be confused within the same year.
The table lists ₹500 and ₹1,000 as affected; the text separately records ₹2,000 introduction.

unpack.example_or_place: 2016 currency change.
unpack.consequence: Aligns the table with the detailed 8 November bullet.
unpack.visual_verb: match
unpack.level_extra: Retain the text’s qualifier 'existing' when explaining the affected notes.

p010-i26.content: Year: 2023 | Government: Narendra Modi | Currency affected: ₹2,000 withdrawn (not demonetised)

teacher_understanding.question: What currency event does the table place in 2023?
teacher_understanding.answer: Under Narendra Modi, ₹2,000 notes were withdrawn, explicitly marked 'not demonetised'.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the parenthetical qualification essential?
teacher_understanding.answer: The accompanying text says the notes remained legal tender, so this row is not a fourth demonetisation.

p010-i28.content: It states that "bad money drives out good money" when both are accepted as legal tender at the same face value.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Gresham’s Law state here?
teacher_understanding.answer: When both monies are legal tender at the same face value, bad money drives good money out of circulation.

teacher_understanding.question: What condition qualifies the slogan on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both must be accepted as legal tender at the same face value; the following bullets add fixed exchange value and intrinsic undervaluation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why would people spend bad money and keep good money?
teacher_understanding.answer: If both settle the same payment but one contains more valuable material, people have an incentive to spend the less intrinsically valuable money and retain, melt or otherwise remove the more valuable money from ordinary circulation.

teacher_understanding.question: How should bad and good be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They refer to relative intrinsic value under the legal valuation, not necessarily counterfeit versus genuine or physically dirty versus clean notes.

p010-i28.exam_note: The conditional mechanism matters more than the slogan; good money leaves circulation, not existence.

p010-i31.content: The government fixes their exchange value.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does fixed exchange value matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: A fixed legal valuation can prevent the more intrinsically valuable money from receiving a correspondingly higher payment value, creating an incentive to retain it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the government enter the page’s statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page makes government-fixed exchange value a required condition of the law.

teacher_understanding.question: What if exchange values can adjust to intrinsic worth?
teacher_understanding.answer: The stated mechanism may not operate in the same way because the more valuable money can command a higher exchange value instead of being legally undervalued.

p010-i31.exam_note: Fixed legal valuation is a key qualification of the slogan.

p010-i32.content: One currency is undervalued relative to its intrinsic value.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does intrinsic undervaluation drive good money out?
teacher_understanding.answer: If money’s material worth exceeds what its legal valuation recognises relative to the other money, spending it sacrifices value that can be preserved by retaining it.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this condition complete the mechanism?
teacher_understanding.answer: Legal equivalence creates a choice, and the intrinsic-value mismatch makes spending the less valuable money more attractive.

teacher_understanding.question: What mismatch does the page require?
teacher_understanding.answer: One currency must be undervalued relative to its intrinsic value.

teacher_understanding.question: What does drives out mean for the good money?
teacher_understanding.answer: It tends to be withheld from ordinary circulation, not necessarily destroyed or made illegal.

p010-i32.exam_note: Undervalued good money is retained; relatively overvalued bad money circulates.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does freedom to choose the coin matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: The subsequent example depends on people retaining older, purer coins while spending the debased ones.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this choice alter circulation?
teacher_understanding.answer: When the better-metal coin and the poorer-metal coin discharge the same payment, keeping the better-metal coin preserves more metal value without sacrificing purchasing power in that payment.

p011-i1.exam_note: A condition behind the good-money/bad-money mechanism, not an unconditional claim about every currency.

teacher_understanding.answer: Good money is withdrawn by hoarding or melting, whereas bad money is used for payments.

teacher_understanding.question: How is its treatment different?
teacher_understanding.answer: People hoard or melt good money instead of spending it as they do bad money.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can melting or hoarding be attractive?
teacher_understanding.answer: Intrinsic value is the value of the material in the coin. A holder may preserve that metal value by storing the coin or recovering its metal.

p011-i4.exam_note: Good here refers to intrinsic value, not appearance or legal validity.

teacher_understanding.question: Why spend the lower-metal-value coin?
teacher_understanding.answer: If both coins settle the same face-value payment, spending the lower-metal-value one gives up less valuable metal.

p011-i6.content: • England in the 16th century provides the classic example. During the reign of Henry VIII, many silver coins were debased by reducing their silver content.

teacher_understanding.question: When and where did this example occur?
teacher_understanding.answer: In sixteenth-century England during Henry VIII's reign.

teacher_understanding.question: What change was made to the coins?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their silver content was reduced, making them debased silver coins.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does reducing silver content matter for this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reducing precious-metal content lowers the metal value of a coin and creates a difference between purer and debased coins.

p011-i6.exam_note: Historical illustration; understand debasement rather than inventing an unstated policy motive.

teacher_understanding.question: Why were the purer coins hoarded?
teacher_understanding.answer: Old and new coins had the same face value, so people retained the older, purer coins and left mostly debased coins circulating.

teacher_understanding.question: How does equal face value create the incentive?
teacher_understanding.answer: The same stated payment can be made with either coin. Spending the debased coin lets the holder keep more valuable metal in the purer coin.

teacher_understanding.question: What was the circulation outcome?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mostly debased coins remained in circulation, not necessarily the disappearance of every purer coin.

p011-i7.exam_note: Retain the qualifiers 'same face value' and 'mostly'.

teacher_understanding.question: What is bank or deposit money?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is money held as bank-account deposits, transferred through banking instruments instead of being handed over as cash.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature distinguishes it from physical cash on this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The money exists in an account, and payment uses banking instruments rather than physical cash.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a payment occur without handing over notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank-mediated payment changes the relevant account balances; the transfer instruction is distinct from the deposit money being transferred.

p011-i9.exam_note: Distinguish the deposit from its payment instrument.

terms.everyday_image: फोन पर bank balance दिखना, जेब में उतने नोट न होना

Bank deposits can be transferred through banking instruments.

teacher_understanding.question: What role does bank money have in modern money supply?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies it as the largest component of modern money supply.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page provide a percentage or dated data?
teacher_understanding.answer: No; it gives a qualitative largest-part claim, without a numerical share.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should students not identify the whole money supply with cash?
teacher_understanding.answer: Money held in transferable bank deposits can support payments even though no notes or coins change hands.

p011-i10.exam_note: No percentage should be inferred from 'largest'.

The page identifies deposit money as the largest part.

p011-i11.content: • Payments can be made through cheques, UPI, debit cards, NEFT, RTGS, and other banking channels.

teacher_understanding.question: Which payment means does the page list?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cheques, UPI, debit cards, NEFT and RTGS, together with other banking channels.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this list differ from the Act's three instruments?
teacher_understanding.answer: The payment-channel list includes UPI, debit cards, NEFT and RTGS; the Act discussion lists promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these channels relate to bank money?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide ways to initiate or carry out payment using bank deposits; the deposit is the money, while the channel enables its use.

teacher_understanding.question: What is UPI, and where would a learner use it?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface. It enables instant payments between bank accounts through participating apps. Scanning a shopkeeper's QR code and authorising payment is a familiar use.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a debit card enable payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: A debit card accesses funds in its linked bank account. When used to pay at a shop or online, the payment draws on that account rather than providing a credit-card-style borrowing facility. It can also be used to withdraw cash at an ATM.

teacher_understanding.question: What is NEFT, and how are its transfers processed?
teacher_understanding.answer: NEFT stands for National Electronic Funds Transfer. It transfers funds between bank accounts through settlement in batches at half-hourly intervals. A familiar use is sending money to another person's bank account using account details and an IFSC.

teacher_understanding.question: What is RTGS, and how is its settlement different?
teacher_understanding.answer: RTGS stands for Real Time Gross Settlement. Transfers are settled individually, transaction by transaction, in real time rather than being accumulated into batches. It is used for large-value account transfers, such as a substantial business payment.

teacher_understanding.question: What does 'gross' add to 'real time' in RTGS?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Real time' concerns processing without waiting for a later batch; 'gross' means each transfer is settled individually rather than being combined with other transfers for net settlement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should instant UPI payment and RTGS not be treated as identical descriptions?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI describes an interface enabling instant payments; RTGS identifies a settlement system characterised by real-time, individual gross settlement. An instant customer payment does not by itself establish that the transaction uses RTGS.

teacher_understanding.question: How should an exam statement matching these four channels to their defining features be checked?
teacher_understanding.answer: Match UPI with instant app-enabled payments, debit cards with access to linked account funds, NEFT with batch settlement, and RTGS with individual real-time gross settlement. A statement assigning batch processing to RTGS reverses the distinction. These channels should not be classified as negotiable instruments merely because they enable payment.

prerequisites: settlement as completion of a funds transfer
p011-i11.exam_note: Test acronym expansions and correct feature matching: UPI—instant payment interface; debit card—linked account funds; NEFT—batches; RTGS—individual real-time gross settlement. Do not equate payment channels with negotiable instruments.

p011-i13.content: o A negotiable instrument is a written document that promises or orders payment of a specified sum and can be transferred from one person to another.

teacher_understanding.question: What is a negotiable instrument?
teacher_understanding.answer: A transferable written document containing a promise or an order to pay a specified sum.

teacher_understanding.question: Which identifying features does the definition supply?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is written, concerns a specified payment, uses a promise or order, and can pass from one person to another.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'negotiable' not simply bargaining over price?
teacher_understanding.answer: Here the word concerns transfer of the instrument and the associated payment right, not haggling over how much to pay.

p011-i13.exam_note: Promise versus order, specified sum and transferability are statement-test features.

The instrument records a specified promise or order and can be transferred.

unpack.consequence: Creates a shared definition for the three instruments.
