teacher_understanding.answer: No. 'Allowed' expresses permission, and 'upto ₹50' gives a ceiling in the printed statement rather than a compulsory flat charge.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish a fee ceiling from an actual fee?
teacher_understanding.answer: A permitted maximum does not by itself establish what a particular bank or channel actually charges.

p014-i21.exam_note: Preserve 'allowed', 'upto' and 'sender'; not a verified current universal tariff.

terms.plain_meaning: बताई गई अधिकतम fee ₹50 तक, जरूरी नहीं कि हर बार पूरे ₹50 हों
terms.everyday_image: अधिकतम कीमत लिखी हो तो उससे कम भी लिया जा सकता है

why_chain.step: A sender needs to know the cost beyond the transferred amount.
The page mentions permission for a sender fee upto ₹50.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking a bank's fee schedule before initiating RTGS.
unpack.consequence: Do not transform a permission ceiling into a compulsory charge.
unpack.visual_verb: cap a sender-fee bar at ₹50
unpack.level_extra: No date, channel distinction or full tariff schedule is supplied.

teacher_understanding.question: What does IMPS stand for?
teacher_understanding.answer: Immediate Payment Service, presented here as a system for immediate transfers.

teacher_understanding.question: Which page features explain 'Immediate'?
teacher_understanding.answer: The prose says 'Immediate transfer', and the table calls its speed instant and its primary use urgent everyday transfers.

teacher_understanding.question: How should IMPS be distinguished from mobile banking?
teacher_understanding.answer: IMPS is the payment service; mobile banking is one access channel through which a customer can use it.

p014-i22.exam_note: Expansion and association with NPCI, immediacy and everyday transfers.

terms.plain_meaning: पैसे तुरंत भेजने की payment सुविधा
terms.everyday_image: किसी को जरूरत पड़ने पर phone से तुरंत पैसे भेजना

why_chain.step: An everyday payment can be urgent even when it is not high-value.
The table assigns urgent everyday transfers to IMPS.

unpack.example_or_place: An urgent transfer using a banking app.
unpack.consequence: IMPS supplies another instant option distinct from RTGS and UPI.
unpack.visual_verb: expand IMPS and move an everyday payment immediately
unpack.level_extra: Mobile access is not synonymous with UPI.

teacher_understanding.question: What amount range does the IMPS prose give?
teacher_understanding.answer: It gives ₹1 to a maximum of ₹5 lakhs.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the table qualify or differ from that range?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its maximum is 5 lakh with the qualification 'varies by bank', while its minimum says 'No minimum', unlike the prose's ₹1 starting point.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should both ends of an amount range be checked?
teacher_understanding.answer: A transfer must fit applicable lower and upper conditions; remembering just the maximum can obscure other eligibility or channel restrictions.

p014-i23.exam_note: ₹5 lakh and bank-wise qualification; retain the minimum discrepancy.

terms.plain_meaning: बताई गई सबसे बड़ी भेजी जा सकने वाली रकम
terms.everyday_image: रकम बढ़ाने वाला slider एक सीमा पर रुकना

why_chain.step: A user needs to know whether an intended transfer fits the allowed range.
The prose gives ₹1–₹5 lakhs; the table adds bank variation to the maximum.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking the transfer screen's permitted amount before confirming IMPS.
unpack.consequence: Read the prose range alongside the table qualification.
unpack.visual_verb: mark ₹1 and ₹5 lakhs on a range bar
unpack.level_extra: Do not silently replace the prose's ₹1 with the table's 'No minimum'.

p014-i24.content:
• Immediate transfer.
• Available round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: What speed and availability are claimed for IMPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides immediate transfers and is available round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the table express these claims?
teacher_understanding.answer: The Speed row says 'Instant', and Availability says '24×7, all days'.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both immediacy and round-the-clock access useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: An urgent payment outside branch hours needs both the ability to initiate it then and a fast processing route; one feature alone does not imply the other.

p014-i24.exam_note: Both speed and availability differ conceptually even when both favour convenience.

terms.plain_meaning: दिन हो या रात, पूरे समय सुविधा मिलना
terms.everyday_image: रात को जरूरत पड़ने पर भी payment शुरू करना

why_chain.step: Urgent payment needs do not stop at branch closing time.
IMPS is described as immediate and available round the clock.

unpack.example_or_place: An urgent account transfer in the evening.
unpack.consequence: Supports the urgent everyday-transfer use case.
unpack.visual_verb: send a payment across a day-and-night clock
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer NEFT-like batching from the shared 24×7 availability.

p014-i25.content: • Works through mobile and internet banking.

teacher_understanding.question: Which access channels does the prose name for IMPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mobile banking and internet banking.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the table add an access channel?
teacher_understanding.answer: Yes. It lists ATMs as well as mobile and internet banking.

teacher_understanding.question: How can internet banking and mobile banking access the same payment service?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank website and a bank app are different customer interfaces that can submit instructions to the same underlying payment arrangement.

p014-i25.exam_note: Include the image-only ATM entry when learning IMPS channels.

terms.plain_meaning: bank की phone सुविधा या website से account का काम करना
terms.everyday_image: bank की app और browser में bank की website

why_chain.step: A customer needs a way to submit a transfer instruction.
The prose names mobile and internet banking; the table also lists ATMs.

unpack.example_or_place: Selecting IMPS within a bank's transfer menu.
unpack.consequence: The device or app alone does not determine the payment system.
unpack.visual_verb: join several access channels to IMPS
unpack.level_extra: Read prose and table together for complete channel coverage.

p014-i26.exam_note: Section transition; BBPS is not explained on this page.

p014-i27.where_on_page: bottom, below AEPS and BBPS heading

teacher_understanding.question: What does AEPS stand for?
teacher_understanding.answer: Aadhaar Enabled Payment System; the expansion identifies Aadhaar as its distinguishing link.

teacher_understanding.question: How much does this page establish about AEPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies the name and expansion only. It does not yet explain transactions, authentication or limits.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'Aadhaar Enabled' first be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It indicates a payment arrangement in which Aadhaar supports access or identification, rather than naming a new form of money. The detailed mechanism needs a separate explanation.

p014-i27.exam_note: Learn the expansion; avoid importing unsupported operational details into this page's content.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस सुविधा में Aadhaar की मदद से पहचान या पहुँच जुड़ी हो
terms.everyday_image: पहचान बताकर किसी सुविधा तक पहुँचना

why_chain.step: A payment facility needs a way to identify or connect its user.
The expansion names Aadhaar as the enabling link.

unpack.example_or_place: The new AEPS section beginning at the bottom of this page.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the learner for the following explanation without inventing missing details.
unpack.visual_verb: expand AEPS and highlight Aadhaar
unpack.level_extra: BBPS remains a heading-only reference here.

p015-i1.content: Enables banking transactions using Aadhaar and biometrics, primarily for financial inclusion.

teacher_understanding.question: How does AEPS identify a user for banking transactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies Aadhaar and biometrics as the means used for transactions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can this support financial inclusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Biometric identity verification at a nearby service point can reduce dependence on travelling to a branch or using a card and PIN, helping people access banking services.

p015-i1.exam_note: Associate AEPS with Aadhaar and biometrics, not with a bill-payment platform.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की पहचान वाली खासियत से पहचान जाँचना
terms.everyday_image: fingerprint देकर पहचान की जाँच

terms.plain_meaning: जिन लोगों तक banking नहीं पहुँचती, उन्हें भी उससे जोड़ना
terms.everyday_image: गाँव के व्यक्ति को पास में banking सुविधा मिलना

why_chain.step: Some people face distance and access barriers to banking.
AEPS uses Aadhaar and biometrics primarily to support financial inclusion.

unpack.example_or_place: A village resident using an Aadhaar-enabled banking service point.
unpack.consequence: Connect identity verification with access to banking, then locate the Bank Mitra's role.
unpack.visual_verb: verify identity and open access
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish identity authentication from the source of money in an account.

p015-i2.content: Authentication and payment is done via Bank Mitras.

teacher_understanding.question: How are AEPS authentication and payment accessed according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are carried out through Bank Mitras, who provide the local service interface.

teacher_understanding.question: When does authentication matter in this service?
teacher_understanding.answer: Identity is checked when the customer requests a transaction, before the transaction is authorised.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use a Bank Mitra rather than require a branch visit?
teacher_understanding.answer: A bank's local representative can bring assisted banking closer to people who have difficulty reaching or using a branch.

p015-i2.exam_note: Bank Mitra is the service intermediary; do not confuse the intermediary with NPCI.

terms.plain_meaning: bank की ओर से लोगों को पास में banking सेवा देने वाले प्रतिनिधि
terms.everyday_image: गाँव की दुकान पर banking सहायता का counter

why_chain.step: A distant branch can make routine banking difficult.
Bank Mitras provide the authentication and payment interface described here.

unpack.example_or_place: An assisted transaction at a local Bank Mitra point.
unpack.consequence: Financial inclusion requires a usable local access point as well as an identity system.
unpack.visual_verb: connect customer to bank through an agent
unpack.level_extra: Keep the customer-facing agent distinct from the payment-system operator.

p015-i3.content: Helps in Direct Benefits Transfer, helping government subsidies reach the grassroots levels.

teacher_understanding.question: How is AEPS linked to subsidy delivery?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says it supports Direct Benefits Transfer and helps government subsidies reach grassroots beneficiaries.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does access to banking matter after a benefit has been transferred?
teacher_understanding.answer: A credit in an account is useful only if the recipient can access or use it; a nearby assisted banking point can help bridge this last-mile gap.

p015-i3.exam_note: Distinguish DBT as benefit delivery from AEPS as a banking-access mechanism.

terms.plain_meaning: सरकार का लाभ सीधे लाभ पाने वाले तक पहुँचाना
terms.everyday_image: सरकारी मदद की रकम beneficiary के account में पहुँचना

why_chain.step: A beneficiary needs practical access to a government benefit, not merely an account entry.
AEPS helps government subsidies reach grassroots levels.

unpack.example_or_place: A beneficiary accessing a credited subsidy through a local banking point.
unpack.consequence: Links payment infrastructure to welfare implementation.
unpack.visual_verb: trace benefit to beneficiary
unpack.level_extra: Do not describe AEPS itself as a subsidy scheme.

p015-i4.exam_note: Expansion is developed in the following item.

p015-i5.content: Provides a single interoperable platform for paying bills such as electricity, mobile, gas, insurance, etc.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Bharat Bill Payment System provide?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides a common interoperable platform for paying different kinds of bills, including electricity, mobile, gas and insurance.

teacher_understanding.question: Which examples show that BBPS is not limited to one utility?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page lists electricity, mobile, gas and insurance bills.

teacher_understanding.question: How does interoperability help the payer?
teacher_understanding.answer: Participating billers and payment channels can work through common arrangements, reducing the need for an isolated payment route for each biller.

p015-i5.exam_note: Interoperable bill payments are the defining clue; the examples are not an exhaustive list.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग जुड़े systems का आपस में काम कर पाना
terms.everyday_image: एक payment रास्ते से अलग-अलग bill भरना

why_chain.step: Households have bills from several different providers.
BBPS brings multiple bill categories onto a single interoperable platform.

unpack.example_or_place: Paying electricity and mobile bills through a participating payment channel.
unpack.consequence: Separates bill-payment infrastructure from AEPS identity-based banking access.
unpack.visual_verb: converge several bills onto one platform
unpack.level_extra: A common platform does not mean that there is only one customer-facing app.

p015-i6.content: NPCI manages both AEPS and BBPS.

teacher_understanding.question: Which common institution manages the two systems named here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page attributes management of both AEPS and BBPS to NPCI.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the page's explicit institutional link between AEPS and BBPS?
teacher_understanding.answer: A separate bold sentence states that NPCI manages both.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should common management not make a student treat them as the same service?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their functions on the page differ: AEPS supports Aadhaar-biometric banking, while BBPS supports interoperable bill payments.

p015-i6.exam_note: Useful institution–product matching fact; retain the page's management wording.

terms.plain_meaning: कई payment systems से जुड़ी संस्था
terms.everyday_image: एक संस्था के नीचे अलग-अलग काम करने वाले payment रास्ते

why_chain.step: Different payment needs require different systems.
The page gives AEPS and BBPS a common manager, NPCI.

unpack.example_or_place: An institution–system matching question.
unpack.consequence: Introduces the same institution before RuPay and e-RUPI.
unpack.visual_verb: branch NPCI into two named systems
unpack.level_extra: Common institutional parent does not imply identical purpose.

teacher_understanding.question: Which year does the page associate with RuPay's introduction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heading gives 2012.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a domestic card payment system significant?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides a domestic card-network option rather than leaving card payments dependent solely on foreign networks.

p015-i7.exam_note: Link RuPay to 2012; the book uses 'payment gateway' terminology.

why_chain.step: Card payments need a network connecting participating institutions.
The page places RuPay's introduction in 2012 and describes it as domestic.

unpack.example_or_place: A RuPay-branded bank card.
unpack.consequence: Anchors the later product features in time.
unpack.visual_verb: place RuPay at 2012
unpack.level_extra: Outside clarification: RuPay is a card payment network; 'network' and a merchant payment gateway are not technically identical.

p015-i8.content: Rupee + Payment = RuPay card. It was launched by NPCI.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the name RuPay combine, and who launched it?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page combines Rupee and Payment to explain the name and identifies NPCI as the launcher.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the plus-and-equals expression establish?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the page's name mnemonic, not a numerical payment formula.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the mnemonic be used in an exam?
teacher_understanding.answer: Use it to remember the brand, while keeping the institution–product link, NPCI–RuPay, separate from the wordplay.

p015-i8.exam_note: NPCI–RuPay matching is more important than the name mnemonic.

why_chain.step: A brand name needs to be linked to its institution.
The page supplies both the Rupee–Payment mnemonic and NPCI as launcher.

unpack.example_or_place: NPCI → RuPay on a revision chart.
unpack.consequence: Connects RuPay to the institutional theme of the page.
unpack.visual_verb: join Rupee and Payment into RuPay
unpack.level_extra: The symbols + and = indicate word combination here; they have no units.

p015-i9.content: It is world’s 7th payment gateway similar to Mastercard, Visacard [Visa card], China’s Union Pay.

teacher_understanding.question: Which systems does the page compare with RuPay?
teacher_understanding.answer: It places RuPay alongside Mastercard, Visa and China's Union Pay as similar payment systems, while calling RuPay the world's seventh payment gateway.

teacher_understanding.question: What domestic identity distinguishes RuPay in the adjacent text?
teacher_understanding.answer: The next bullet identifies RuPay specifically as India's domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the seventh-place description be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: As an attributed book claim, not as proof of a current ranking by transaction volume, size or quality; this page supplies no such criterion.

p015-i9.exam_note: Retain the named comparators; avoid turning an unsupported ordinal into a current market-share ranking.

why_chain.step: Students need familiar comparators to identify RuPay's role.
The page compares it with Mastercard, Visa and Union Pay.

unpack.example_or_place: Different network logos printed on bank cards.
unpack.consequence: Places RuPay in the card-payment family, not among currencies.
unpack.visual_verb: align card-network logos
unpack.level_extra: The book's gateway wording is broader than the technical card-network distinction.

p015-i10.content: Rupay charges less fees than other companies and is India’s domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: What fee comparison does the book make?
teacher_understanding.answer: It says RuPay charges lower fees than other companies, without specifying the fee category or amount.

teacher_understanding.question: What national identity does the page assign RuPay?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes RuPay as India's domestic payment system.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can lower payment-processing costs matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: They can reduce the cost burden of accepting and processing electronic payments and encourage participation.

p015-i10.exam_note: Lower fees do not mean all transactions and cards are free.

terms.plain_meaning: अपने देश का payment system
terms.everyday_image: भारत के bank card पर RuPay का निशान

why_chain.step: Payment services involve processing costs.
The book presents RuPay as a lower-fee domestic option.

unpack.example_or_place: Merchant card acceptance and bank card processing.
unpack.consequence: Explains the economic relevance of the domestic-system claim.
unpack.visual_verb: compare fee bars
unpack.level_extra: No numeric fee, fee payer or universal zero-fee rule is stated.

p015-i11.content: Types of Cards: RuPay debit, credit, and prepaid cards.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three RuPay card types are listed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Debit, credit and prepaid cards.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these types differ by source of spending funds?
teacher_understanding.answer: Debit generally draws on account funds; credit uses an approved borrowing limit repaid later; prepaid uses value loaded in advance.

teacher_understanding.question: How can all three still be RuPay cards?
teacher_understanding.answer: The network brand and the funding arrangement are separate dimensions: the same network can support different card products.

p015-i11.exam_note: Reject the statement that RuPay is exclusively a debit card.

terms.plain_meaning: खर्च का पैसा अपने account से कटता है
terms.everyday_image: खरीदारी के बाद bank balance कम होना

terms.plain_meaning: अभी उधार की limit से खर्च, बाद में चुकाना
terms.everyday_image: महीने के अंत में card bill भरना

terms.plain_meaning: पहले से भरी रकम से खर्च करना
terms.everyday_image: पहले recharge, फिर इस्तेमाल

why_chain.step: People may pay from savings, borrowing or preloaded value.
RuPay includes debit, credit and prepaid cards.

unpack.example_or_place: Compare account balance, credit limit and loaded value.
unpack.consequence: Prepares learners to distinguish the PMJDY debit-card point from RuPay credit-card linkage.
unpack.visual_verb: split RuPay into three funding types
unpack.level_extra: Classify by source of funds, not by the shared network logo.

p015-i12.content: Rupay debit card given free with PMJDY (Jan Dhan) Bank account.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card is associated with a Jan Dhan account here?
teacher_understanding.answer: A RuPay debit card, described as given free with the PMJDY account.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the page promise a free RuPay credit card with PMJDY?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. The specific product named is a debit card.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a debit card help turn account ownership into usable access?
teacher_understanding.answer: It gives the account holder a way to access account funds through supported card facilities rather than relying solely on branch counters.

p015-i12.exam_note: The trap is replacing 'debit' with 'credit' or reading free card provision as free money.

terms.plain_meaning: लोगों को banking से जोड़ने वाली Jan Dhan account योजना
terms.everyday_image: नए account के साथ RuPay debit card मिलना

why_chain.step: Opening an account should be followed by ways to use its funds.
The page links a free RuPay debit card to Jan Dhan accounts.

unpack.example_or_place: A Jan Dhan account holder's RuPay debit card.
unpack.consequence: Connects RuPay to the financial-inclusion theme introduced through AEPS.
unpack.visual_verb: attach debit card to Jan Dhan account
unpack.level_extra: PMJDY expands to Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (outside clarification).

p015-i13.content: One of India's major payment innovations is linking RuPay Credit Cards to UPI.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card–platform linkage is highlighted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page highlights linking RuPay credit cards to UPI.

teacher_understanding.question: Which card type is explicitly named in this innovation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Credit cards, not merely the RuPay debit cards mentioned in the preceding bullet.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the learner understand a card linked to UPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: UPI becomes the payment interface while the linked credit card is the funding source for eligible payments; interface and funding source are different layers.

p015-i13.exam_note: Do not generalise the line into universal eligibility for every card or every UPI transaction.

terms.term: linking RuPay Credit Cards to UPI
terms.plain_meaning: UPI से payment करते समय जुड़ा RuPay credit card इस्तेमाल करना
terms.everyday_image: QR payment के पीछे credit card का funding रास्ता

why_chain.step: A familiar payment interface can connect to different funding sources.
The page identifies RuPay credit-card linkage to UPI as an innovation.

unpack.example_or_place: An eligible merchant payment through UPI using a linked RuPay credit card.
unpack.consequence: Sets up the distinction between UPI as infrastructure and e-RUPI as a voucher built using it.
unpack.visual_verb: link credit card to UPI
unpack.level_extra: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface (outside clarification).

p015-i14.content: Vertical RuPay country graphic: six flag-and-country entries, top to bottom Bhutan, Nepal, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates, Singapore and Maldives. Each flag is paired with a country name and a statement about RuPay issuance or acceptance. There are no arrows or route connections.
p015-i14.type_note: The image proposal was none; this inset contains teachable visual country information.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the inset show?
teacher_understanding.answer: It pairs six countries with specific RuPay card issuance or acceptance claims.

teacher_understanding.question: Which countries appear?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bhutan, Nepal, Mauritius, United Arab Emirates, Singapore and Maldives.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should issuance and acceptance be read separately?
teacher_understanding.answer: Issuance means making cards available through an issuer; acceptance means allowing their use at supported payment or cash-access points. One does not automatically establish the other.

p015-i14.exam_note: Read country-specific wording; this is not a uniform claim of issuance in all six countries.

terms.plain_meaning: ग्राहक को नया card जारी करना
terms.everyday_image: bank से नया card मिलना

terms.plain_meaning: उस जगह card से लेन-देन हो पाना
terms.everyday_image: दुकान की machine पर card चल जाना

why_chain.step: A domestic card system may also have overseas use arrangements.
The inset gives different country-specific issuance and acceptance facts.

unpack.example_or_place: An Indian traveller checking supported overseas card facilities.
unpack.consequence: Domestic origin does not mean use is confined to India.
unpack.visual_verb: pair each flag with its distinct claim
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer acceptance at every outlet or treat the list as exhaustive or current.

p015-i15.where_on_page: right inset, first entry beside Bhutan flag
p015-i15.content: BHUTAN — First country to issue RuPay cards (2020). Accepted at ATMs and merchants.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinctive Bhutan claim does the inset make?
teacher_understanding.answer: It names Bhutan as the first country to issue RuPay cards in 2020 and states acceptance at ATMs and merchants.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the date and acceptance channels given?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are printed in the first flag entry, beside Bhutan.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'first country' be understood in this international inset?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the overseas-issuance milestone in context, not a claim that RuPay originated in Bhutan rather than India.

p015-i15.exam_note: Pair Bhutan with the 2020 issuance milestone; avoid losing the overseas context.

why_chain.step: International reach can involve issuing cards as well as accepting them.
Bhutan's entry records both an issuance milestone and acceptance channels.

unpack.example_or_place: Bhutan: ATMs and merchants.
unpack.consequence: Differentiate this issuance milestone from Mauritius's 2024 entry.
unpack.visual_verb: pin 2020 to Bhutan
unpack.level_extra: Read the first-country claim in the foreign-country inset's context.

p015-i16.where_on_page: right inset, second entry beside Nepal flag
p015-i16.content: NEPAL — Accepted at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What facilities are named for Nepal?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay acceptance at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this entry give a Nepal card-issuance date?
teacher_understanding.answer: No; it gives acceptance channels, unlike the dated issuance entries.

teacher_understanding.question: How does PoS use differ from ATM use?
teacher_understanding.answer: A PoS terminal supports merchant payment, while an ATM provides banking functions such as cash withdrawal.

p015-i16.exam_note: Nepal is an acceptance entry, not a dated issuance entry.

terms.plain_meaning: दुकान पर card से payment लेने वाली machine
terms.everyday_image: किराने की दुकान की card machine

why_chain.step: Travellers need to know where a card can be used.
Nepal's entry identifies ATMs and PoS terminals.

unpack.example_or_place: Nepal, supported ATM or shop terminal.
unpack.consequence: Shows both cash-access and purchase-payment channels.
unpack.visual_verb: connect Nepal to ATM and shop icons
unpack.level_extra: PoS expands to Point of Sale (outside clarification).

p015-i17.where_on_page: right inset, third entry beside Mauritius flag
p015-i17.content: MAURITIUS — RuPay card issuance started in 2024.

teacher_understanding.question: What Mauritius milestone is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay card issuance started in 2024.

teacher_understanding.question: Is this entry about issuance or named acceptance locations?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly concerns card issuance and supplies a year, not a list of ATM or merchant channels.

teacher_understanding.question: Why not automatically add ATM acceptance to this entry?
teacher_understanding.answer: Issuance and acceptance are different claims, and evidence for one should not be treated as proof of every channel of the other.

why_chain.step: Overseas development includes local issuance milestones.
The Mauritius entry dates issuance to 2024.

unpack.example_or_place: Mauritius, 2024 issuance milestone.
unpack.consequence: Adds a later date to the RuPay chronology.
unpack.visual_verb: pin 2024 to Mauritius
unpack.level_extra: Do not convert an issuance fact into an unstated universal acceptance claim.

p015-i18.where_on_page: right inset, fourth entry beside UAE flag
p015-i18.content: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES — Accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What acceptance channels are stated for the UAE?
teacher_understanding.answer: ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Does the UAE entry include an issuance year?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Its printed claim is acceptance at those two types of facilities.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a merchant terminal relate to card use?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the merchant-side device used to initiate and process a card payment.

why_chain.step: An overseas card user needs supported access points.
The UAE entry names ATMs and merchant terminals.

unpack.example_or_place: UAE, supported ATM or merchant terminal.
unpack.consequence: Extends the domestic system's stated overseas reach.
unpack.visual_verb: pair UAE flag with two acceptance icons
unpack.level_extra: Supported acceptance is not a promise that every terminal accepts the card.

p015-i19.where_on_page: right inset, fifth entry beside Singapore flag
p015-i19.content: SINGAPORE — Accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the Singapore acceptance claim?
teacher_understanding.answer: RuPay is accepted at ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other inset entry uses the same channel wording?
teacher_understanding.answer: The United Arab Emirates entry also says ATMs and merchant terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the channel wording important?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies where the card may be used rather than claiming that local card issuance has started.

p015-i19.exam_note: Do not attach Bhutan's or Mauritius's issuance dates to Singapore.

why_chain.step: Foreign use depends on acceptance arrangements.
Singapore's entry names ATM and merchant-terminal acceptance.

unpack.example_or_place: Singapore, supported ATM or merchant terminal.
unpack.consequence: Reinforces the acceptance-versus-issuance distinction.
unpack.visual_verb: pair Singapore with ATM and merchant icons
unpack.level_extra: Treat as the book's snapshot, not a live coverage guarantee.

p015-i20.where_on_page: right inset, last entry beside Maldives flag
p015-i20.content: MALDIVES — Accepted at ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: What channels are named for Maldives?
teacher_understanding.answer: ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: Which entry has the same channel wording?
teacher_understanding.answer: Nepal also lists ATMs and PoS terminals.

teacher_understanding.question: How should these two channels be distinguished?
teacher_understanding.answer: An ATM is a banking access device; a PoS terminal is used at a merchant to take payments.

p015-i20.exam_note: Maldives appears in the image even though it is absent from native text.

why_chain.step: Card users need both cash-access and shopping-payment information.
The Maldives entry lists ATMs and PoS terminals.

unpack.example_or_place: Maldives, supported ATM or shop terminal.
unpack.consequence: Completes all six entries in the graphic.
unpack.visual_verb: connect Maldives flag to two facilities
unpack.level_extra: An acceptance entry does not itself supply an issuance date.

teacher_understanding.question: Which year and institution are attached to e-RUPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: The heading associates it with NPCI and 2021.

teacher_understanding.question: Why introduce a purpose-restricted electronic voucher?
teacher_understanding.answer: Such a voucher can direct funded assistance toward a specified service rather than provide unrestricted spending money.

p015-i21.exam_note: Link 2021 and NPCI to e-RUPI; do not confuse the name with a digital rupee.

why_chain.step: A sponsor may want to fund a particular service.
The following text presents e-RUPI as a person- and purpose-specific voucher.

unpack.example_or_place: The page's vaccination voucher example.
unpack.consequence: Moves from general payment infrastructure to targeted service delivery.
unpack.visual_verb: place e-RUPI at 2021
unpack.level_extra: Contrast the RuPay 2012 and e-RUPI 2021 dates.

p015-i22.where_on_page: first e-Rupi bullet and repeated first bullet near bottom
p015-i22.content: E-Rupi is an SMS /QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher created by National Payment Corporation of India [National Payments Corporation of India] (NPCI) using its UPI Platform. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: What is e-RUPI according to the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a prepaid cashless electronic voucher delivered through SMS or QR code, created by NPCI using its UPI platform.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words establish the instrument and its delivery form?
teacher_understanding.answer: The definition calls it a 'Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher' and specifies 'SMS /QR Code'.

teacher_understanding.question: How do prepaid, cashless and electronic fit together?
teacher_understanding.answer: Prepaid means value is funded in advance; cashless means redemption does not require handing over cash; electronic means the entitlement is represented digitally rather than as a paper coupon.

p015-i22.exam_note: Separate the voucher from its delivery medium and underlying platform.

terms.plain_meaning: पहले से रकम तय किया हुआ digital coupon, जिससे cash दिए बिना तय सेवा ली जाए
terms.everyday_image: फोन पर आया पहले से paid service coupon

terms.plain_meaning: फोन के message या scan होने वाले code से voucher मिलना
terms.everyday_image: फोन पर message या चौकोर scan code

why_chain.step: A sponsor needs a way to deliver funded service entitlement.
E-RUPI supplies a prepaid electronic voucher through SMS or QR code.

unpack.example_or_place: A ₹1,000 vaccination voucher sent to a phone.
unpack.consequence: Using UPI infrastructure does not make the voucher itself an ordinary UPI app.
unpack.visual_verb: send funded voucher to phone
unpack.level_extra: Correct NPCI's expansion to National Payments Corporation of India; SMS is Short Message Service and QR is Quick Response (outside clarification).

p015-i23.where_on_page: second e-Rupi bullet and its repetition
p015-i23.content: It is not a payment app, bank transfer, or digital currency. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: Which three things is e-RUPI explicitly distinguished from?
teacher_understanding.answer: A payment app, a bank transfer and digital currency.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a restricted voucher differ from unrestricted account money or currency?
teacher_understanding.answer: A voucher represents an entitlement subject to stated redemption conditions rather than general spending power in the recipient's account or a currency instrument.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does an SMS or QR form not make it a payment app?
teacher_understanding.answer: SMS and QR describe delivery or presentation; an app is software used as an interface. The form in which an entitlement arrives does not determine its economic category.

p015-i23.exam_note: High-value statement trap: e-RUPI is not the digital rupee or a cryptocurrency.

why_chain.step: Similar digital names can hide different types of instruments.
The page excludes apps, bank transfers and digital currency from e-RUPI's definition.

unpack.example_or_place: A service coupon compared with money credited freely into an account.
unpack.consequence: Focus classification on what can be redeemed, not on the digital appearance.
unpack.visual_verb: separate voucher from app, transfer and currency
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate e-RUPI with e₹ merely because both names refer to the rupee.

p015-i24.where_on_page: third e-Rupi bullet and its repetition
p015-i24.content: Instead, it is a person-specific and purpose-specific voucher that can only be used by the intended beneficiary for the intended service. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: What two restrictions define e-RUPI here?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is tied to the intended beneficiary and to the intended service.

teacher_understanding.question: Which wording rules out general spending?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page says 'person-specific and purpose-specific' and restricts use to the intended beneficiary and service.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are both restrictions needed for targeted assistance?
teacher_understanding.answer: A person restriction addresses who receives the benefit; a purpose restriction addresses what the benefit buys. Either alone leaves the other targeting question unresolved.

p015-i24.exam_note: Remember both axes: intended person AND intended purpose.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस व्यक्ति के लिए है, उसी के इस्तेमाल के लिए
terms.everyday_image: किसी एक नाम का service coupon

terms.plain_meaning: जिस काम के लिए मिला है, उसी काम में इस्तेमाल
terms.everyday_image: vaccination का coupon, grocery खरीदने का पैसा नहीं

why_chain.step: A sponsor may need to ensure both the right recipient and the right service.
E-RUPI is restricted on both person and purpose.

unpack.example_or_place: The intended beneficiary redeeming a vaccination voucher.
unpack.consequence: Explains why cash withdrawal or spending elsewhere is excluded in the example.
unpack.visual_verb: lock voucher to a person and a service
unpack.level_extra: The two restrictions are separate conditions, not synonyms.

p015-i25.content: Think of it as a digital gift coupon with restrictions. (Printed twice.)

teacher_understanding.question: How does the gift-coupon analogy help explain e-RUPI?
teacher_understanding.answer: It makes the voucher understandable as a prepaid entitlement that is presented to obtain an allowed service.

teacher_understanding.question: What limits the ordinary gift-coupon analogy?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page specifies person and purpose restrictions; it is not describing an unrestricted gift of spending money.

teacher_understanding.question: Why keep the word 'restrictions' in the analogy?
teacher_understanding.answer: Without it, learners might incorrectly assume that the recipient can spend the value on any purchase or pass it around freely.

p015-i25.exam_note: Useful memory aid, but the formal restrictions determine correctness.

terms.plain_meaning: फोन वाला coupon, पर इस्तेमाल की तय शर्तों के साथ
terms.everyday_image: एक खास सेवा के लिए मिला coupon

why_chain.step: An unfamiliar digital instrument needs a familiar everyday comparison.
The page uses a restricted digital gift coupon as that comparison.

unpack.example_or_place: A coupon that pays for a service but cannot be converted into shopping cash.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the learner for the numerical vaccination example.
unpack.visual_verb: transform gift coupon into restricted digital voucher
unpack.level_extra: An analogy explains the idea; it does not remove beneficiary or purpose conditions.

p015-i26.where_on_page: indented vaccination example and partial repeated example at bottom
p015-i26.content: Suppose the government wants to pay for your COVID vaccination costing ₹1,000. Instead of transferring ₹1,000 into your bank account, it sends you an e-RUPI voucher worth ₹1,000 via SMS or QR code. You can redeem it only for vaccination at an authorized center—not withdraw cash or spend it elsewhere. The first two sentences are repeated at the bottom of this page; the repeated redemption sentence continues on the next page.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the vaccination example work?
teacher_understanding.answer: The government funds a ₹1,000 vaccination benefit, sends a voucher of that value through SMS or QR code instead of crediting the recipient's account, and the beneficiary redeems it for vaccination at an authorised centre.

teacher_understanding.question: When and where may the beneficiary use the voucher in this example?
teacher_understanding.answer: When obtaining the specified vaccination at an authorised centre; the example excludes cash withdrawal and unrelated spending.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does sending a ₹1,000 voucher differ from transferring ₹1,000 to an account?
teacher_understanding.answer: The voucher constrains the use of the funded benefit, whereas an ordinary unrestricted account credit does not itself impose that vaccination-only redemption condition.

teacher_understanding.question: Is ₹1,000 a general e-RUPI limit or an announced universal vaccination benefit?
teacher_understanding.answer: No such rule is stated. The text begins 'Suppose', making ₹1,000 the illustrative cost and voucher value in this example.

p015-i26.exam_note: ₹ means Indian rupees; ₹1,000 is illustrative, not a stated statutory limit. Do not treat the example as an actual scheme announcement.

terms.plain_meaning: voucher दिखाकर उसके बदले तय सेवा लेना
terms.everyday_image: vaccination centre पर coupon देकर सेवा लेना

terms.plain_meaning: वह centre जहाँ इस voucher के बदले सेवा लेने की अनुमति है
terms.everyday_image: तय centre पर coupon मान्य होना

why_chain.step: The government in the hypothetical example wants to pay for vaccination, not unrelated purchases.
It sends a ₹1,000 voucher redeemable only for vaccination at an authorised centre.

unpack.example_or_place: Government → ₹1,000 SMS/QR voucher → intended beneficiary → authorised vaccination centre.
unpack.consequence: Shows person-and-purpose targeting in action and why a voucher is not unrestricted cash.
unpack.visual_verb: send voucher, redeem service, block cash and unrelated purchases
unpack.level_extra: Track sponsor, beneficiary, value, delivery medium, provider and permitted use separately.

p016-i1.content: You can redeem it only for vaccination at an authorized center—not withdraw cash or spend it elsewhere.

teacher_understanding.question: What can the voucher in the continued example be used for?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its permitted use is vaccination at an authorized center. Cash withdrawal and spending elsewhere are excluded.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words establish both purpose and place restrictions?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Only for vaccination' specifies the purpose, while 'at an authorized center' specifies the permitted place of redemption.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does this differ from receiving unrestricted cash?
teacher_understanding.answer: A purpose-restricted voucher directs purchasing power toward a specified service, whereas unrestricted cash can generally be spent across many purposes.

prerequisites: A voucher as a claim to a specified benefit
p016-i1.exam_note: Distinguish purpose-specific redemption from cash transfer; do not infer the instrument's name from this page alone.

terms.plain_meaning: voucher दिखाकर उसके बदले तय सेवा लेना
terms.everyday_image: कूपन देकर तय सामान लेना, नकद पैसे नहीं

terms.plain_meaning: वह जगह जिसे यह सेवा देने की मंजूरी मिली है
terms.everyday_image: टीका लगवाने के लिए मंजूर किए गए केंद्र पर जाना

why_chain.step: The benefit in this example is intended for vaccination.
Restricting redemption prevents treating the voucher as freely spendable cash.

unpack.example_or_place: Vaccination at an authorized center in the continued example.
unpack.consequence: A voucher's stated value does not imply a right to withdraw that value as cash.
unpack.visual_verb: Allow redemption at the vaccination center; block cash withdrawal and unrelated shopping.
unpack.level_extra: Watch statements that equate a purpose-specific voucher with unrestricted money.

p016-i2.type_note: This is a section heading, not a numerical claim despite the word 'Rate'.

p016-i3.content: MDR is the fees that a merchant must pay to his (acquirer) bank for every card transaction.

teacher_understanding.question: What does MDR mean in a card payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the transaction fee payable by the merchant to the acquiring bank, rather than the amount paid for the goods themselves.

teacher_understanding.question: What identifies the payer, recipient, and occasion for MDR?
teacher_understanding.answer: The definition names the merchant as payer, the acquirer bank as recipient, and each card transaction as the occasion.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a merchant receive less than the customer's purchase amount?
teacher_understanding.answer: Payment acceptance involves services supplied by payment participants; a transaction fee can be deducted from the sale proceeds before the merchant receives the net amount.

prerequisites: A bank account receiving sale proceeds
p016-i3.exam_note: Core definition; 'discount' here is not a shopping discount given to the customer.

terms.plain_meaning: card payment लेने पर दुकानदार से लगने वाली fee
terms.everyday_image: दुकान की पूरी बिक्री में से payment की fee कटना

terms.plain_meaning: दुकानदार की तरफ card payment लेने वाला bank
terms.everyday_image: दुकान के payment counter के पीछे काम करने वाला bank

why_chain.step: The merchant needs a way to accept a customer's card payment.
The book identifies MDR as the merchant's fee for that transaction.

unpack.example_or_place: A shop accepting a card payment; the diagram below uses ₹1,000.
unpack.consequence: Gross purchase value and the merchant's net receipt can differ.
unpack.visual_verb: Separate the sale amount from the payment-processing fee.
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret 'discount' as a customer concession or assume the illustrated 2% is universal.

p016-i4.content:
The merchant does not pay the entire MDR to one entity. It is shared among:
Acquiring Bank (merchant's bank)
Issuing Bank (customer's bank)
Card Network (RuPay, Visa, Mastercard, etc.)
Payment Service Provider/Gateway, where applicable

teacher_understanding.question: Which participants share MDR?
teacher_understanding.answer: The acquiring bank, issuing bank, card network, and, where applicable, payment service provider or gateway share it. The merchant's payment to the acquirer does not mean the acquirer keeps the whole fee.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the acquiring and issuing banks situated in the transaction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The acquiring bank is on the merchant's side; the issuing bank is the customer's bank. RuPay, Visa, and Mastercard are listed separately as card networks.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these roles differ in a typical card payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: The acquirer supports merchant acceptance, the issuer supplies and authorizes the customer's card facility, the network carries transaction messages between participants, and a gateway can provide the connection through which payment information is submitted.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the phrase 'where applicable' be retained?
teacher_understanding.answer: The list makes the provider or gateway's inclusion conditional rather than saying that this participant receives a share in every transaction.

p016-i5.content: The merchant pays MDR, not the customer.

teacher_understanding.question: Who bears the MDR charge as stated here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The merchant is the identified payer of MDR; the customer is not identified as its payer.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the diagram support this statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: The customer pays ₹1,000, but the merchant receives ₹980 at 2% MDR, locating the deduction on the merchant's receipt.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish the purchase payment from MDR?
teacher_understanding.answer: Paying for goods and paying a payment-acceptance fee are different obligations. The customer's purchase amount should not be confused with the merchant's processing charge.

p016-i6.content: A left-to-right flow connects Customer → Merchant → Banks & [and] Payment Network. The first arrow says 'Pays ₹1,000'; the second says 'MDR shared'. Beneath the flow: 'Merchant receives ₹980 when MDR = 2%'. The fee is therefore ₹20 in this example.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the payment flow illustrate?
teacher_understanding.answer: It follows a ₹1,000 customer payment to the merchant and shows MDR being shared with banks and the payment network, leaving ₹980 for the merchant.

teacher_understanding.question: Which amounts are gross payment and net merchant receipt?
teacher_understanding.answer: ₹1,000 is the customer's gross purchase payment; ₹980 is the merchant's receipt at the illustrated 2% MDR.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the ₹20 difference calculated?
teacher_understanding.answer: Two percent means 2 per 100: ₹1,000 × 2/100 = ₹20. Subtracting ₹20 from ₹1,000 gives ₹980.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should the arrows not be read as the complete banking settlement procedure?
teacher_understanding.answer: This is a simplified allocation picture. It identifies who pays and who shares the fee rather than showing every authorization, clearing, and settlement step.

p016-i6.exam_note: Illustrative calculation, not a claim that MDR is universally 2%.

p016-i14.where_on_page: first Project Nexus bullet and its lower repetition
p016-i14.content:
It is a multilateral cross-border payments initiative led by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub that aims to connect the fast payment systems (FPS) of different countries,
[The same bullet is printed again in the lower section.]

teacher_understanding.question: What is Project Nexus?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is an initiative for connecting fast payment systems across countries through multilateral cooperation, led by the BIS Innovation Hub.

teacher_understanding.question: What establishes its leadership and international scope?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page explicitly names the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub and says it aims to connect FPS of different countries.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'multilateral cross-border' be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Multilateral' means involving several countries rather than just a pair. 'Cross-border' refers to payments between countries rather than within one country.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the project connect systems rather than merely name payment apps?
teacher_understanding.answer: Domestic payment systems already serve their own users; interoperability creates a way for payments to move between those national arrangements.

prerequisites: A payment system connecting payers and payees
p016-i14.exam_note: Leadership, multilateral character, and connection of FPS are key correct-statement facts.

Objective: Allowing people to send money internationally as easily as making a domestic UPI payment.
[Printed twice on this page.]

teacher_understanding.question: What familiar activity is used as the benchmark for international transfers?
teacher_understanding.answer: The book uses the ease of making a domestic UPI payment as the desired benchmark for sending money internationally.

teacher_understanding.question: What remains different between the two kinds of payment?
teacher_understanding.answer: A domestic payment stays within one country's setting; an international payment must work across national payment arrangements.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this objective relate to the project's design?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page's standardized connection between national instant payment systems is the proposed way to simplify international money transfers.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this an objective rather than proof of identical service conditions?
teacher_understanding.answer: The wording describes the ease the project seeks to achieve; it does not supply measured transfer times, costs, or an assurance that all international transfers already match domestic UPI.

p016-i15.exam_note: Distinguish stated aim from proven universal availability, speed, or zero cost.

p016-i17.where_on_page: Project Nexus, existing-transfer problem bullet and its lower repetition
p016-i17.content:
Today, sending money abroad usually involves multiple correspondent banks, higher fees, and delays.
[Printed twice on this page.]

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page present a need for simpler cross-border payments?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes the usual overseas-transfer arrangement as involving several correspondent banks, higher fees, and delays.

teacher_understanding.question: How can correspondent banks make a transfer possible?
teacher_understanding.answer: When the sending and receiving banks do not have a direct arrangement, other banks can provide intermediate account and payment relationships through which the transfer is routed.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can extra intermediaries add time and cost?
teacher_understanding.answer: Additional institutions can introduce processing steps, checks, and charges. This explains the problem without claiming every overseas transfer follows the same route.

teacher_understanding.question: Does 'usually' mean all international payments necessarily use many banks?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. The page describes a common pattern rather than an exceptionless rule.

p016-i17.exam_note: Understand the problem Nexus addresses; retain the qualifier 'usually'.

p016-i18.where_on_page: below the country table, standardized connection bullet
p016-i18.content: Project Nexus creates a single standardized connection between national instant payment systems, so countries do not need to build separate payment links with every other country.

teacher_understanding.question: How does Nexus change the connection problem?
teacher_understanding.answer: A standardized connection between national instant payment systems replaces the need for each country to construct separate links with every other country.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is a shared connection approach useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Without common arrangements, each additional bilateral link may require separate technical coordination. A common connection model reduces repeated integration work.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'single standardized connection' be understood without overreading it?
teacher_understanding.answer: It means a common way of connecting systems, like using an agreed interface, rather than proof that countries abolish their own domestic systems.

teacher_understanding.question: What practical consequence does the page explicitly state?
teacher_understanding.answer: Countries no longer need to build a separate payment link with every other country for this connectivity model.

p016-i18.exam_note: Central design logic: multilateral standardized connectivity versus repeated country-to-country links.

p017-i1.content: Project Nexus creates a single standardized connection between national instant payment systems, so countries do not need to build separate payment links with every other country.

teacher_understanding.question: What problem does the standardised connection address?
teacher_understanding.answer: It avoids the need for countries to build a separate payment link with each other country.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a shared standard simplify connecting payment systems?
teacher_understanding.answer: A system can connect through a common set of technical rules rather than designing a different interface for each foreign partner. This is interoperability between systems, not the creation of one common currency.

p017-i1.exam_note: Distinguish a standardised payment connection from a common currency or separate bilateral links.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग payment systems को जोड़ने का एक जैसा तय तरीका
terms.everyday_image: अलग phones के लिए एक ही तरह का charger port

why_chain.step: Separate links require separate connection arrangements with partners.
Project Nexus provides a standard connection instead of separate country-by-country links.

unpack.example_or_place: A national instant payment system connecting with systems abroad.
unpack.consequence: Interoperability can expand without rebuilding a unique link for each partner.
unpack.visual_verb: replace many pairwise links with standardised connections
unpack.level_extra: Ask whether the arrangement connects payment systems or replaces national currencies.

p017-i2.content: Plastic Currency Notes by the RBI

p017-i3.content: These are the currency notes made from security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP) instead of the traditional cotton-based paper substrate.

teacher_understanding.question: What defines these plastic currency notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their underlying material is security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene, abbreviated BOPP, rather than cotton-based paper.

teacher_understanding.question: Which material contrast establishes the distinction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page explicitly contrasts BOPP with the traditional cotton-based paper substrate.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner understand 'substrate' and 'biaxially oriented'?
teacher_understanding.answer: The substrate is the base sheet carrying the printing and security features. Biaxial orientation means the polymer film is stretched in two directions during manufacture to improve its properties.

prerequisites: material used as a printing base
p017-i3.exam_note: Know the full form of BOPP and the cotton-based-paper comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: दो दिशाओं में खींचकर तैयार की गई खास polymer film
terms.everyday_image: दो ओर से तानी गई पतली sheet

terms.plain_meaning: वह आधार sheet जिस पर note बनता और छपता है
terms.everyday_image: जिस कागज़ पर तस्वीर छपती है

why_chain.step: A banknote needs a suitable base to carry printing and withstand handling.
The page identifies security-grade BOPP as the alternative to cotton-based paper.

unpack.example_or_place: The material forming the body of a physical banknote.
unpack.consequence: Plastic currency refers to a change of banknote material, not a digital payment instrument.
unpack.visual_verb: swap cotton-based sheet for polymer film
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse polymer notes with plastic payment cards.

p017-i4.content: They are specially engineered polymer banknotes with embedded security features, not ordinary plastic.

teacher_understanding.question: How do polymer banknotes compare with ordinary plastic?
teacher_understanding.answer: The banknotes are specially engineered and incorporate security features; the page rejects treating them as ordinary plastic.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes being made of plastic insufficient for a currency note?
teacher_understanding.answer: A banknote must also be recognisable and verifiable as genuine currency, not merely be a sheet of polymer.

teacher_understanding.question: Why embed security features in a note?
teacher_understanding.answer: Features that are difficult to reproduce help users and machines distinguish genuine notes from counterfeits.

p017-i4.exam_note: Material and built-in security both matter; ordinary plastic is not equivalent to a banknote.

terms.plain_meaning: असली note पहचानने की खास चीज़ें जो उसके भीतर या बनावट में हों
terms.everyday_image: कपड़े में बुना हुआ पहचान का निशान

why_chain.step: Currency needs protection against copying.
These polymer notes contain specially engineered security features.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking the authenticity of a banknote before accepting it.
unpack.consequence: The material change also serves the anti-counterfeiting objective.
unpack.visual_verb: reveal security features within the note
unpack.level_extra: The page does not list particular security features; do not invent a list as book content.

p017-i5.content: RBI will start with small denomination notes such as ₹10 and ₹20. Up to 4x longer time span.

teacher_understanding.question: Which denominations and durability claim does the page give?
teacher_understanding.answer: It states a proposed start with ₹10 and ₹20 notes and a lifespan of up to four times longer.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this sentence prove that polymer notes have already been issued nationally?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. It uses the prospective wording 'will start' and provides no implementation date or evidence of actual nationwide issuance.

teacher_understanding.question: Why would low denominations be useful for assessing durability?
teacher_understanding.answer: Frequently used low-value notes pass through many hands, making resistance to everyday wear especially relevant.

p017-i5.exam_note: Retain ₹10, ₹20 and 'up to 4x'; do not convert a proposed rollout into a completed event.

terms.plain_meaning: कम face value वाले notes
terms.everyday_image: छुट्टे में दिया गया ₹10 का note

why_chain.step: Repeated handling wears down notes.
The page proposes low denominations and claims up to fourfold longevity.

unpack.example_or_place: Small-value cash changing hands at a shop.
unpack.consequence: Longer life could mean fewer replacements, not a higher face value.
unpack.visual_verb: compare note lifetimes on parallel timelines
unpack.level_extra: 'Up to' is an upper-bound claim, not a guaranteed lifespan for every note.

p017-i6.content: 2013: Government approved a field trial of ₹10 polymer notes.

teacher_understanding.question: When did the government approve the stated field trial?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page dates approval of a ₹10 polymer-note field trial to 2013.

teacher_understanding.question: Why conduct a field trial before wider adoption?
teacher_understanding.answer: Testing in actual use can reveal durability, handling and acceptance problems that laboratory checks may not capture.

teacher_understanding.question: How does approval differ from completed implementation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Approval authorises a trial; it does not by itself establish that the trial was completed or that nationwide circulation followed.

p017-i6.exam_note: Pair 2013 with approval of a ₹10 field trial, not nationwide replacement.

terms.plain_meaning: असल इस्तेमाल की जगह पर सीमित जाँच
terms.everyday_image: नई bus को पहले एक route पर चलाकर देखना

why_chain.step: A new note material must work under everyday conditions.
A field trial provides practical testing before a wider decision.

unpack.example_or_place: 2013 approval concerning ₹10 polymer notes.
unpack.consequence: Separate the policy milestone from claims about actual circulation.
unpack.visual_verb: mark approval on a timeline
unpack.level_extra: Approval, trial completion and nationwide launch are distinct milestones.

p017-i7.content: Existing paper notes will continue to circulate alongside polymer notes; this is not a currency replacement exercise.

teacher_understanding.question: What relationship does the page envisage between paper and polymer notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both would circulate alongside one another rather than polymer notes replacing the existing paper currency in this exercise.

teacher_understanding.question: How is introducing a new material different from withdrawing existing notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: A new material can be added while old notes remain usable. Withdrawal instead changes the acceptability or circulation status of existing notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must a learner keep these ideas separate?
teacher_understanding.answer: A change in what a note is made of does not itself imply cancellation of the older note's monetary status.

p017-i7.exam_note: Avoid equating polymer-note introduction with demonetisation.

terms.plain_meaning: दोनों तरह के notes का साथ-साथ लेन-देन में चलना
terms.everyday_image: wallet में पुराने और नए design के notes साथ रखना

why_chain.step: Changing a note material need not invalidate existing money.
The page explicitly retains paper notes alongside polymer notes.

unpack.example_or_place: A cash payment using either form of note.
unpack.consequence: Coexistence, not compulsory replacement, is the stated approach.
unpack.visual_verb: place paper and polymer notes side by side
unpack.level_extra: A statement asserting immediate paper-note withdrawal contradicts this page.

p017-i8.content: The main objective is to make Indian currency last longer, become harder to counterfeit, and reduce replacement costs.

teacher_understanding.question: What three problems is the change meant to address?
teacher_understanding.answer: The objectives are longer note life, greater difficulty of counterfeiting and lower replacement costs.

teacher_understanding.question: How can longer note life reduce replacement costs?
teacher_understanding.answer: When notes remain fit for use for longer, fewer worn-out notes need to be printed, transported and replaced over a given period.

teacher_understanding.question: Does harder to counterfeit mean impossible to counterfeit?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Greater resistance raises the difficulty of copying; it is not a guarantee that copying cannot occur.

p017-i8.exam_note: Three objectives; distinguish reduced replacement costs from a claim of lower initial manufacturing cost.

terms.plain_meaning: असली जैसा दिखने वाला नकली note बनाना
terms.everyday_image: असली label की नकल करके नकली सामान बेचना

why_chain.step: Worn-out notes require replacement and fake notes undermine trust.
Durability and security are intended to reduce replacement needs and copying.

unpack.example_or_place: The currency-management work of replacing unfit notes.
unpack.consequence: The rationale combines efficiency with trust in cash.
unpack.visual_verb: slow wear, block copying and shrink replacement piles
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer counterfeit-proof currency or reduced face value.

p017-i9.content: More than 50 countries use polymer banknotes. Australia was the 1st country to introduce them in 1988.

teacher_understanding.question: Which first introduction and date does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies Australia as the first country to introduce polymer banknotes, in 1988.

teacher_understanding.question: What scale of international adoption is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page states that more than 50 countries use polymer banknotes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is international adoption relevant to this discussion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Experience in other countries can inform assessment of durability, security and practical use; it does not automatically prove that every country should adopt the same design.

p017-i9.exam_note: Remember Australia–1988; the country count is an undated page claim.

why_chain.step: A proposed material change raises questions about practical experience.
The page cites Australia's introduction and use by more than 50 countries as international context.

unpack.example_or_place: Australia, 1988.
unpack.consequence: Polymer banknotes are presented as an internationally used technology.
unpack.visual_verb: mark Australia and extend an adoption timeline
unpack.level_extra: First introduction does not mean every Australian note was converted in that same year.

p017-i11.content: It is a digital / virtual currency created & stored using blockchain technology.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the page mean by cryptocurrency?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes a digital or virtual currency using blockchain technology rather than physical notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Which technology is explicitly named in the definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blockchain is the technology the page associates with its creation and storage.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a blockchain help explain digital ownership?
teacher_understanding.answer: It records transactions in linked blocks maintained under shared verification rules. The ledger records ownership or control; it is not a warehouse holding physical coins.

p017-i11.exam_note: Digital money is a broader category; not every digital payment is cryptocurrency.

terms.plain_meaning: लेन-देन के records को जुड़े हुए blocks में रखने का तरीका
terms.everyday_image: हिसाब के जुड़े पन्ने, जिनका पिछला हिसाब अगले से जुड़ा हो

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी currency जो physical note की जगह digital रूप में हो
terms.everyday_image: हाथ में सिक्का नहीं, screen पर दर्ज balance

why_chain.step: A digital asset needs a dependable record of transactions and control.
Blockchain supplies linked records governed by verification rules.

unpack.example_or_place: A cryptocurrency transfer recorded on its blockchain.
unpack.consequence: The next distinction is who creates the asset and whether it is legal tender.
unpack.visual_verb: link transaction blocks
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate a bank transfer or UPI payment with cryptocurrency.

p017-i12.content: It is a privately created digital asset. It is not legal tender in India and is not issued by the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: What institutional and legal status does the page assign to cryptocurrency?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is privately created, not issued by the RBI and not legal tender in India.

teacher_understanding.question: Which statements rule out treating this asset as RBI-issued currency?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page explicitly identifies private creation and says it is not issued by the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'not legal tender' different from 'illegal'?
teacher_understanding.answer: Legal tender is a legal status concerning settlement of monetary obligations. Lacking that status does not by itself settle whether holding or trading an asset is prohibited.

teacher_understanding.question: How is an RBI digital currency different on this criterion?
teacher_understanding.answer: A central bank digital currency is issued by the central bank, unlike a privately created cryptocurrency.

p017-i12.exam_note: High-value traps: private crypto versus CBDC, and not legal tender versus illegal.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसे कानून पैसे की देनदारी चुकाने के लिए मान्यता देता है
terms.everyday_image: उधार चुकाने में कानून से मान्यता पाया भुगतान

why_chain.step: Something may be owned or traded without having the status of official money.
The page separates private crypto from RBI issuance and Indian legal-tender status.

unpack.example_or_place: Comparing a privately created crypto asset with central-bank money.
unpack.consequence: Digital form alone does not confer official currency status.
unpack.visual_verb: separate issuer and legal-status columns
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer a blanket ban or a tax rule from this sentence.

p017-i13.content: It relies on a distributed ledger to record ownership without a central authority like a bank or government.

teacher_understanding.question: What performs the ownership-recording function?
teacher_understanding.answer: A distributed ledger records ownership without a central authority such as a bank or government.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the records maintained in a distributed ledger?
teacher_understanding.answer: Copies are maintained across participating network computers rather than in a single central institution's record system.

teacher_understanding.question: How can participants agree without a central bookkeeper?
teacher_understanding.answer: The network follows agreed validation and consensus rules to decide which transactions and ledger updates are accepted.

teacher_understanding.question: Does decentralised recording mean there are no rules?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Removing a central bookkeeper makes shared verification rules important; decentralisation is not the absence of governance or checks.

p017-i13.exam_note: Understand distributed records versus a central bank or bank-maintained ledger.

terms.plain_meaning: हिसाब की ऐसी किताब जिसकी copies network में कई जगह रखी जाती हैं
terms.everyday_image: एक ही साझा खर्च का हिसाब कई दोस्तों के पास

why_chain.step: Without a central bookkeeper, participants still need an agreed ownership record.
Distributed records and validation rules provide a way to maintain that agreement.

unpack.example_or_place: Network computers maintaining matching transaction histories.
unpack.consequence: Trust shifts from one institution toward network rules and verification.
unpack.visual_verb: replicate and synchronise ledger copies
unpack.level_extra: A distributed ledger is the record arrangement; consensus is how updates are agreed.

p017-i14.exam_note: Introduces motivations rather than a practice question.

p017-i15.where_on_page: first indented bullet under Why Cryptocurrency
p017-i15.content: Some anarchist groups lost faith in FIAT MONEY because USA’s Subprime Crisis (2007) eroded the purchasing power of US Dollar.
p017-i15.type_note: The 2007 date supports a claimed motive for distrust; the sentence's main content is causal, not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: What motive for cryptocurrency interest does the page attribute to some anarchist groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page attributes their loss of faith in fiat money to the USA's 2007 subprime crisis and its claimed erosion of dollar purchasing power.

teacher_understanding.question: How can distrust of financial institutions make decentralised money attractive?
teacher_understanding.answer: People who distrust official issuers or intermediaries may prefer a system whose ownership records do not depend on those institutions.

teacher_understanding.question: What do fiat money, purchasing power and subprime crisis mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fiat money derives monetary standing from state authority rather than redemption into a commodity. Purchasing power is how much goods and services money buys. The subprime crisis involved risky mortgage lending and defaults that damaged the financial system.

teacher_understanding.question: What caution is needed about the historical explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: A financial crisis can undermine institutional trust, but its effect on a currency's purchasing power is not a single automatic relationship. The page supplies no evidence establishing its specific dollar-purchasing-power claim, and the motivation should not be generalised to every crypto user.

p017-i15.exam_note: Know fiat money and the trust argument; treat the page's crisis narrative as an attributed simplification.

terms.plain_meaning: सरकारी मान्यता से चलने वाला पैसा, जिसे सोने में बदलने का वादा ज़रूरी नहीं
terms.everyday_image: note की कीमत उसके कागज़ की कीमत से कहीं अधिक होना

terms.plain_meaning: पैसे से कितनी चीज़ें खरीदी जा सकती हैं
terms.everyday_image: ₹100 में पहले और अब मिलने वाला राशन

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसे समूह जो राज्य की central authority का विरोध करते हैं
terms.everyday_image: एक central controller के बजाय खुद नियम तय करने की चाह

terms.plain_meaning: कमज़ोर repayment क्षमता वाले borrowers के housing loans से जुड़ा financial संकट
terms.everyday_image: कई उधार एक साथ न लौटें तो उधार देने वाला भी मुश्किल में

why_chain.step: Some people distrust official money and financial intermediaries after financial disruption.
A system without a central institutional bookkeeper may appeal to them.

unpack.example_or_place: The page's reference to the USA's 2007 subprime crisis.
unpack.consequence: Connect the motivation to decentralised ownership recording, without treating it as the sole origin of crypto.
unpack.visual_verb: trace distrust toward an alternative ledger
unpack.level_extra: Separate financial-system trust, domestic purchasing power and exchange value; they are not identical.

p017-i16.where_on_page: second indented bullet under Why Cryptocurrency
p017-i16.content: They also dislike Banks & Card Companies because of transaction charges on e-banking, card payments, MDR, interoperability issues.

teacher_understanding.question: What other dissatisfaction does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It cites transaction charges on e-banking and card payments, MDR and interoperability problems as reasons for disliking banks and card companies.

teacher_understanding.question: How do MDR and interoperability affect everyday payments?
teacher_understanding.answer: MDR, Merchant Discount Rate, is the merchant-side charge associated with accepting card payments. Interoperability concerns whether different payment systems can work with one another; poor compatibility can limit where or how payments are made.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this criticism prove that cryptocurrency payments have no costs or compatibility issues?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Cryptocurrency networks may also have transaction fees, technical constraints and compatibility problems. The paragraph describes a motivation, not a guarantee of a cost-free alternative.

p017-i16.exam_note: Know MDR and interoperability; do not infer that crypto transactions are free.

terms.plain_meaning: card payment लेने पर merchant से लिया जाने वाला charge
terms.everyday_image: ग्राहक के payment में से दुकान को मिलने वाली रकम पर कटौती

terms.plain_meaning: अलग payment systems का आपस में काम कर पाना
terms.everyday_image: एक system से दूसरे system के ग्राहक को payment पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Charges and incompatible systems create payment friction.
The page presents this friction as another motive for seeking alternatives.

unpack.example_or_place: A merchant accepting a customer's card payment.
unpack.consequence: Links cryptocurrency motivations back to the page's opening concern with connected payment systems.
unpack.visual_verb: show a fee deduction and an incompatible connection
unpack.level_extra: MDR is not simply the interest charged on a credit-card loan.

p017-i18.content: Money supply is the total amount of money available in an economy at a given point in time that people and businesses can use for spending, saving, or making payments.
